World.title: Pregnant woman found dead by roadside in Kirinyaga with head, hip injuries
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The National Police Service (NPS) has launched investigations after the body of a pregnant woman was found by the roadside in the Itangi area of Mwea East Sub-County, Kirinyaga County.

The woman, identified as Catherine Njeru, was found early Friday morning along the Piai-Itangi Murram Road with visible injuries to her head and hip.

In a statement, NPS said the incident is being investigated as a suspected murder.

"The NPS condoles with the family, relatives, and friends of the deceased and commits to expeditious and conclusive investigations to ensure that any person or persons responsible for this barbaric crime are brought to justice," read the statement.

Police have urged residents of Itangi to remain calm and refrain from speculation as the investigation continues.

Anyone with information that could assist the investigation has been asked to report to the nearest police station or a law enforcement officer.

The matter is being investigated by Kirinyaga County Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) officers, local Sub-County police and Central Regional Police Command, led by the Regional Criminal Investigations Officer.

According to NPS, the Inspector General of the National Police Service has also been briefed on the incident and directed the Director of Criminal Investigations to expedite the probe and establish the facts surrounding the woman's death.

World.title: Ruto downplays rivalry over oil refinery in East Africa
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former Nigeria President Olesugun Obasanjo, Ali Dangote, President William Ruto and Uganda President Yoweri Museveni during launch of the Lamu Refinery on September 30, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has played down suggestions of rivalry between Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania over competing refinery projects, saying East Africa’s growing demand for petroleum products can support several facilities across the region.

Speaking during a media interview at State House Mombasa, Ruto said Kenya had no objection to Uganda and Tanzania pursuing their own refinery projects, arguing that the different facilities could complement rather than compete with one another.

“There is no bad blood at all. There is no problem,” Ruto said.

His remarks came a day after he presided over the groundbreaking of the Lamu refinery project, which the government is positioning as a major component of a wider industrial complex on the Kenyan coast.

Ruto said he had discussed Uganda’s plans with President Yoweri Museveni and agreed that Kampala could proceed with a smaller refinery without threatening Kenya’s investment in Lamu.

He said Kenya would even be prepared to buy petroleum products from Uganda if they could reach the Kenyan market at competitive prices.

“If it is manufactured there in Uganda and the oil from that place is near Busia, and it can reach Busia at a lower price, we will buy oil from anywhere and bring it to Busia,” Ruto said.

The President argued that the size of the regional petroleum market meant there was room for more than one refinery.

“This one in Lamu cannot serve all of us; it will be necessary to expand,” he said, adding that East Africa had “enough opportunity” for multiple facilities.

Ruto also extended the same approach to Tanzania, saying Kenya could participate in a refinery project in Tanga if it is eventually developed.

“Even if the one in Tanga is built, we as Kenya will go and buy some shares there. There is no problem,” he said.

The comments point to a regional energy market in which petroleum products could move across borders depending on availability, transport costs and prices. Rather than treating refinery projects as competing national investments, Ruto said the facilities could strengthen economic cooperation within the East African Community.

The President said the Lamu refinery would also address some of the challenges Kenya faces from dependence on imported refined petroleum products.

“Lamu will give us an opportunity to have fuel without the fluctuations that we have now,” he said.

He linked the proposed refinery to the need to reduce Kenya’s exposure to international oil price shocks, disruptions caused by instability in oil-producing regions and costs associated with transporting petroleum products over long distances.

Ruto said local refining could reduce expenses related to insurance and transportation while providing Kenya with greater access to locally processed fuel.

However, he said the larger economic opportunity would extend beyond the refinery itself. The government plans to develop industries around the facility, including petrochemical, chemical and plastics manufacturing.

The refinery could also provide raw materials for industries producing fertiliser and bitumen, potentially reducing reliance on imports of some petroleum-based products.

The broader development is expected to create opportunities for employment, investment and trade while strengthening Lamu’s position as an industrial and logistics centre.

Ruto said Kenya’s policy would be guided by competitiveness, allowing businesses and consumers to obtain petroleum products from whichever regional facility can supply them efficiently and at favourable prices.

The President maintained that Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania therefore did not need to view their refinery plans through the lens of rivalry.

Instead, he said, multiple facilities could create a larger and more integrated petroleum market capable of serving the needs of East Africa.

World.title: Outrage as KDF officers detain human rights team along Malindi-Lamu highway
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Activists clashed with police at a Gamba roadblock after being stopped en route to Lamu. [Vocal Africa]

Six members of Muslims for Human Rights (MUHURI), including five staff and a board member, were detained by Kenya Defence Forces (KDF) officers along the Malindi-Lamu highway, prompting condemnation from human rights organisations.

The incident occurred on Monday as the team travelled from Lamu to Mombasa after a field mission. The officers reportedly intercepted them between Gamba and Minjila, detained them for about two hours, then released them.

The Kenya Human Rights Commission (KHRC) and MUHURI said the officers covered their faces and refused to identify themselves when the human rights team challenged them.

The five staff members were identified as Francis Auma, Abdulrahman Mwanga, Fredrick Okado, Lathan Yusuf and Mohamed Abdla, while the board member was identified as Khelef Khalifa.

In a joint statement, the two organisations said the officers' actions violated a High Court ruling by Justice Bahati Mwamuye requiring security personnel to wear clearly visible name tags or identifiable service numbers on their uniforms.

The ruling also prohibits security officers from wearing hoods, balaclavas or face masks to conceal their identities.

"We call on the KDF and other security agencies to comply with the court order. Officers who violate the directive should be held accountable and face legal consequences," the joint statement read in part.

The organisations also demanded immediate compliance with a recent court order lifting the dusk-to-dawn curfew that had been imposed for more than a decade along the Minjila-Lamu highway.

They argued that the curfew had created conditions for arbitrary stops, harassment and detention of travellers using the route, citing the detention of the MUHURI team as an example.

The organisations urged security agencies to respect court orders and protect the rights of travellers using the highway.

However, a senior Anti-Terror Police officer aware of the incident told The Standard that the officers from the Border Police Unit (BPU) manning such roadblocks and tactical borders conceal their faces to protect their identities.

"In high-risk areas prone to insurgent or terrorist retaliation, including Kanyoyo in Kitui heading to Garissa, Moyale and Lamu, anonymity is framed as a matter of personal and operational survival," she stated.

World.title: Kalonzo signals at working with Ruto if 2027 poll is free and fair
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County on September 27, 2026. [Clinton Ambujo, Standard]

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka has signalled that the Opposition could accept the outcome of the 2027 General Election and consider working with President William Ruto if he wins through a free and fair contest.

Speaking at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County, Kalonzo said the political class must commit itself to democratic competition and be prepared to accept the verdict of voters.

“If you beat us, we will have to consider if you have behaved yourself, and if we beat you, we have to look at all these things,” he said.

The Wiper leader also called for stronger democratic institutions, warning against political confrontation that could deepen divisions in the country.

“We have a nation here. We have to make this country truly democratic. I do not think we have a shortcut,” he said.

Kalonzo used the church service to make a broader appeal for a united and effective Opposition, saying political leaders had a responsibility to work together in the national interest.

“Kenya needs a functional official opposition; one that is united and does not thrive on disunity. As leaders, we have a responsibility to work together and play our part in fixing this nation,” he said.

He said he had remained in the Opposition even when some political allies moved into government.

“I have stood in the opposition all these years. Even when others joined government, my brother Eugene Wamalwa and I remained steadfast, and we will continue to stand firm,” he said.

Kalonzo also turned his attention to Parliament, claiming that the National Assembly had been “captured” and challenging lawmakers in both Houses to exercise their constitutional responsibilities.

“The National Assembly has been captured. Let this message reach every leader in the National Assembly and the Senate: you have the power to change things, not just to complain later,” he said.

He urged legislators to defend the interests of the people who elected them and to put the country ahead of political considerations.

The former Vice President also defended retired President Uhuru Kenyatta against claims that he is financing the Opposition ahead of the 2027 contest.

Kalonzo argued that presidential campaigns have historically relied on networks of political allies and supporters rather than family resources alone.

“But here we are saying, please let Uhuru rest; he is a retired President. Stop saying he is our financier,” he said.

Kalonzo cited previous presidential campaigns involving Uhuru, former President Mwai Kibaki and Raila Odinga, arguing that major political campaigns require support from friends and associates.

“Even when Uhuru was running for President, or Kibaki and even Raila, no family has enough resources to support a presidential campaign. It is friends who support you,” he said.

He warned that Kenya was at a delicate political moment and urged leaders to avoid actions that could deepen instability.

“We should not allow the country to get to a worse situation than where it is. We are on the edge of a cliff; the country is at a crossroads,” he said.

World.title: ODM delegates reject Sakaja using the party for gubernatorial bid
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi ODM chairman George Aladwa addressing the media over the upcoming ODM nominations in Nairobi. [Collins Oduor, Standard]

Nairobi ODM delegates have resolved to reject and lobby against attempts by some people in President William Ruto's broad-based government to give Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja the ODM ticket in the 2027 gubernatorial race.

Party members, delegates and branch chairpersons met in Makadara, where they agreed that ODM be allowed to field their own candidates instead of the party allowing UDA leaders to vie on the party ticket.

They also resolved to back Makadara MP George Aladwa. With Tutam songs renting the air during the meeting, they also agreed to back President Ruto's re-election.

"Aladwa should be the party's candidate for Nairobi governor, and every candidate should seek the seat through their own political party," said an agitated delegate from Kasarani.

They insisted ODM should not allow an outsider to join the party and use its ticket to contest for the gubernatorial seat, arguing that the ODM ticket should be reserved for a candidate who enjoys the support of its members.

"We will not allow someone from another party to come and vie using ODM while we have our own members. As a party our only candidate is Aladwa," said delegate chairs.

They added that their position follows a series of meetings held across all 17 constituencies in Nairobi, with Makadara being the final constituency to hold its meeting.

They further argued that the Nairobi gubernatorial seat requires a leader with experience and leadership skills, warning ODM members against supporting candidates they believe lack the necessary political and leadership experience.

They also sustained their criticism towards former president Uhuru, alleging that he is undermining the party and dividing it, and they will not allow it.

George Aladwa backed the ODM members' position, saying every politician seeking elective office should do so through their own political party.

The delegates maintained that ODM should protect its identity and ticket, insisting that candidates from outside the party should not be allowed to use the ODM ticket to pursue elective positions when active and loyal members are sidelined.

The delegates are calling on ODM to ensure that the nomination process is free, fair and transparent, giving party members an opportunity to choose the candidate they want to represent them.

World.title: Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya's first commercial drilling
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya’s first commercial drilling. [Courtes]

Kenya has moved closer to commercial oil production after a 1,500 horsepower drilling rig arrived at the Port of Mombasa ahead of its deployment to the South Lokichar Basin in Turkana County.

The GW70 rig, leased by Gulf Energy E&P BV from Great Wall Drilling Company, docked at Kilindini Port on Friday aboard MV Transit Sedanka after sailing from Duqm Port in Oman.

It is expected to be transported to Turkana, where drilling is scheduled to begin on November 1.

“All workstreams at Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ are running to a tight project management schedule, and the project remains on course for First Oil production in December 2026,” Gulf Energy Chief Executive Officer Paul Limoh said.

The arrival marks a step in the commercial development of the South Lokichar Basin, more than a decade after oil was first discovered in Turkana in 2012.

The first phase of the project is expected to produce about 20,000 barrels of crude oil per day, with output projected to rise to 50,000 barrels per day in the second phase.

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) says Kenya is targeting first oil in December 2026, while the first crude exports through the Port of Mombasa are expected in the first quarter of 2027.

The GW70 will undergo commissioning and acceptance checks before drilling begins. Gulf Energy has contracted Baker Hughes for integrated well services and SLB to provide an early production facility for the first phase.

World.title: Two more suspects arrested over lawyer Kyalo Mbobu murder
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The two suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing as detectives pursue additional leads.

Detectives have arrested two more suspects in connection with the fatal shooting of lawyer Kyalo Mbobu, as an intelligence-led operation targeting people linked to the September 9, 2025 murder intensifies.

The two boda boda riders Nicholas Lemiso Naula and Noah Kipkirui Langat were arrested in Nairobi’s Central Business District, following sustained efforts by detectives to trace individuals suspected to have been involved in the killing.

According to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), Lemiso is a boda boda rider who allegedly ferried the main suspect, Police Constable Julius Cheruiyot, to and from the scene of the murder, while Langat was arrested over alleged surveillance on Mbobu before his killing.

"With three suspects now in custody, detectives are intensifying the hunt for other persons suspected to have played a role in the meticulously planned killing," DCI stated.

His arrest comes shortly after detectives arrested Cheruiyot in connection with the killing.

“The dragnet over the fatal shooting of lawyer Kyalo Mbobu has widened, with detectives arresting a second suspect as an intelligence-led operation targeting persons linked to the murder intensifies,” DCI said.

The two suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing as detectives pursue additional leads and seek to identify and arrest other people who may have been involved. The DCI said the operation remains active as investigators work to establish the circumstances surrounding Mbobu’s murder.

“The DCI is leaving no stone unturned in its efforts to unravel the full circumstances surrounding Lawyer Mbobu’s murder and bring all those responsible to justice,” the agency said.

World.title: Egypt secures record hard-currency reserves as overseas transfers spike
World.content:
Egypt’s financial sector achieved its strongest foreign reserve position in six years, boosted by a massive influx of capital from citizens living abroad.

Latest data released by the Central Bank of Egypt reveals that net foreign assets held across the banking system scaled $31.2 billion as of August 2026—a peak figure not seen since 2020.

Driving this capital accumulation is a persistent upward trajectory in overseas worker remittances.

In July 2026 alone, Egyptians abroad sent home nearly $4.5 billion, representing a robust 20.0% surge compared to the $3.8 billion recorded in July 2025.

The steady growth in transfers underscores renewed confidence in official banking channels and provides crucial hard-currency liquidity for Cairo’s broader economic stabilization efforts.

World.title: African Union urges restraint as Egypt, Ethiopia, and Eritrea plunge Horn of Africa into crisis
World.content:
The African Union Commission expressed deep concern regarding the escalating tensions among Ethiopia, Eritrea, and Egypt, emphasizing that it is closely monitoring developments among the three nations.

In an official statement, the AU Commission called on the three member states to exercise maximum restraint and refrain from any actions or statements that could further escalate tensions and undermine peace and stability in the region.

The Commission stressed the paramount importance of dialogue, peaceful negotiations, and diplomatic channels to resolve all outstanding issues, affirming its readiness to support efforts aimed at de-escalating tensions and fostering peaceful resolution among the involved parties.

Emphasis on dialogue and diplomatic channels

The African Union statement underscored that constructive engagement and adherence to regional stability are essential for safeguarding security in the Horn of Africa and the wider continent.

This first official comment from the African Union comes following the mutual expulsion of diplomats between Cairo and Addis Ababa under a 48-hour deadline, alongside Ethiopia’s decision to close its embassy in Asmara, expel Eritrean diplomats, and Eritrea’s subsequent severance of diplomatic ties with Addis Ababa.

World.title: Egypt condemns attack on power station in Medina, Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Egypt expressed its strong condemnation of the attack targeting a power station in Medina, in the sisterly Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

In an official statement, Egypt reiterated its full denunciation of this flagrant violation and the continued attacks and attempts to destabilize the security and stability of the Kingdom, emphasizing that such an approach represents a dangerous escalation that increases tensions across the region as a whole.

Egypt stressed its categorical rejection of any attempts to compromise the security and sovereignty of Saudi Arabia, reaffirming its full solidarity with any measures taken by the Kingdom to maintain its stability and safety.

Cairo renewed its position that the security of Saudi Arabia is an integral part of Arab national security and is inextricably linked to Egyptian national security.

World.title: Saudi Arabia denies rumors of bombing attempt at Al-Masjid al-Haram in Mecca
World.content:
Saudi security authorities in the Holy City of Mecca denied the accuracy of rumors circulating across certain social media platforms alleging that an individual attempted to blow himself up inside the Grand Mosque (Al-Masjid al-Haram).

Saudi security authorities clarified that the incident actually involved the apprehension of an individual for harassing pedestrians and inciting panic and terror among them.

They confirmed that the situation was handled immediately by the competent authorities, and necessary legal actions were taken against him.

Security authorities in the Holy City emphasized the falsehood of the circulating allegations regarding the incident, calling on the public to refrain from spreading rumors or unverified information and highlighting the importance of obtaining news solely from official, accredited sources.

World.title: Egypt and Ethiopia expel diplomats under 48-hour deadline
World.content:
Egyptian–Ethiopian relations entered a new phase of tension on Thursday after Cairo and Addis Ababa mutually declared diplomats from both countries persona non grata, giving them a 48-hour deadline to leave their respective territories.

The developments began when the Ethiopian Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that an Egyptian diplomat was declared persona non grata, notifying the Egyptian Embassy in Addis Ababa of the requirement for him to depart the country within 48 hours.

The Ethiopian Foreign Ministry clarified that the decision was made pursuant to the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, without disclosing the underlying reasons or specifying any particular violation committed by the Egyptian diplomat. In response, Cairo took a reciprocal measure, declaring a counselor at the Ethiopian Embassy in Egypt persona non grata and granting him 48 hours to leave the country. An official Egyptian source described the Ethiopian move as “unfortunate” and “unjustified.”

The source stated, in remarks reported by Egypt’s official news agency, that Cairo has consistently emphasized its strict refusal to interfere in the internal affairs of other nations or comment on events occurring in other countries, including Ethiopia. He stressed that this stance is rooted in respect for international law and the UN Charter.

Cairo criticizes Ethiopian stance

The Egyptian source directed sharp criticism toward the Ethiopian government, arguing that it is attempting to blame external parties for its domestic crises. He noted that the Ethiopian side regularly attributes its failure in managing successive internal files and crises to alleged interference by external actors, in an effort to cover up its recurring domestic troubles.

The Egyptian response contained no reference to specific Ethiopian allegations against the Egyptian diplomat, nor did the memo issued by the Ethiopian Foreign Ministry reveal the direct trigger for declaring him persona non grata.

Concluding his statement, the Egyptian source announced the reciprocal measure taken against the Ethiopian diplomat, stating that Cairo applied the “principle of reciprocity” by declaring the counselor at the Ethiopian Embassy in Egypt persona non grata and giving him a 48-hour deadline to leave the country.

Escalation amidst concurrent regional crisis

The exchange of diplomatic sanctions between Cairo and Addis Ababa coincided with another regional escalation between Ethiopia and Eritrea. On the same day, Addis Ababa announced the closure of its embassy in Asmara and the expulsion of 10 Eritrean diplomats, accusing them of engaging in activities that the Ethiopian Foreign Ministry claimed posed a “direct threat to national security,” granting them 48 hours to depart.

The Ethiopian Foreign Ministry further accused Eritrea of committing “direct and indirect hostile and escalatory acts.” In response, Asmara announced the severance of diplomatic relations with Addis Ababa, reflecting a broadening scope of tension between the two neighboring nations.

World.title: Israeli plane crashes killing pilot during training flight
World.content:
The Israeli Public Broadcasting Corporation announced on Friday that a light Israeli aircraft crashed during a training flight, resulting in the death of its pilot.

Official statements confirmed that the light aircraft crashed during a training flight in the northern region of Wadi Ara, north of Tel Aviv. The crash led to the death of the pilot, while his co-pilot sustained severe injuries.

The Fire and Rescue Authority stated that following verification with Israeli aviation authorities, it was confirmed that the aircraft was on a training flight and was not a private crop-duster helicopter, emphasizing that no pesticide materials were on board.

One crew member was found deceased at the site of the light aircraft crash, while another 34-year-old crew member was rescued and transported to Rambam Hospital in Haifa in critical condition, where he was placed under sedation on a ventilator.

Fire spreads toward residential areas

Meanwhile, the fire resulting from the plane crash expanded from the crash site up the hillside toward residential homes in Kafr Qara.

Fire crews from the Hadera station operated on two fronts simultaneously: extinguishing the burning wreckage of the aircraft and containing the wildfire to prevent it from advancing toward residential areas.

World.title: Manchester City has been found ‘cheating on an industrial scale.’ What comes next?
World.content:
It’s one of the most extraordinary and monumental moments in the history of the Premier League – a story that has threatened and continues to endanger the very integrity of soccer in England.

Manchester City, one of the most successful teams in the world in recent years, has been found guilty of systematically cheating – financially doping its way to dominance for the best part of a decade.

Ever since this issue sprung into public consciousness in 2018 through a series of leaked emails, this saga has rumbled on in the background. But now, the lid has been blown off, and the outcome could be devastating for the club.

On Tuesday, the Premier League – the domestic competition in which City plays – finally broke its silence with a blistering statement that revealed the outcome of an independent commission.

It said the club was guilty of seriously breaching the league’s financial rules “well over 100 individual” times between 2009 and 2018 through a series of “sham” contracts and commercial agreements that helped conceal “the true state of its finances” by disguising what was essentially secret funding from its UAE ownership.

The league also said the club overstated its income by roughly $1.18 billion (£900 million) and understated its expenses by tens of millions, while also trying to cover up its efforts during the investigation.

Manchester City, though, says it has “irrefutable evidence” that proves its innocence and will appeal the verdict.

The club’s primary sponsor Etihad Airways – after which the team’s stadium is named – has also defended City and its relationship, threatening legal action against the Premier League.

Despite not being named in the report, some of which is redacted, Etihad Airways told CNN Sports that the lack of “clarity and transparency, together with the selective disclosure of information, has created damaging implications for Etihad.”

It added: “Etihad will seek the relevant legal counsel on the options and recourse available to protect its interests.”

So, should City’s appeal be unsuccessful and the club is eventually nailed to rights, just how devastating could the punishment be and what will that mean on and off the pitch?

Manchester City’s dominance

To understand the severity of this matter, it’s important to understand the context around the club.

In 2008, Manchester City was bought by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan through the Abu Dhabi United Group.

What is going to happen to Manchester City following the Premier League’s scathing statement Tuesday? Oli Scarff/AFP/Getty Images

Under the new regime, the club saw a total overhaul. Billions were spent on upgrading the team’s stadium, training complex and, more importantly, playing squad. Some of the world’s best soccer stars and managers suddenly started signing for a club that had been languishing in mediocrity for some time.

The result was City becoming one of the most potent forces in the sport, winning three Premier League titles, three League Cups and one FA Cup during the period covered by the charges.

The new era saw history made, creating some of the most iconic moments the league has ever seen and giving its fans memories that would last a lifetime.

That period also provided the foundations for where City currently sits within the top echelons of world soccer – having won the UEFA Champions League back in 2023 and winning four consecutive Premier Leagues from 2021 to 2024.

City fans will be hoping the club avoids some of the worst sanctions that are being discussed as possibilities by social media and pundits. Alex Livesey/Getty Images

Now, though, the independent panel says it was all done illegally – a “sham,” as it said eight times in its redacted findings.

And it’s not as though this is the first time that City has faced allegations of financial misconduct. In 2020, the club was initially banned from European soccer for two seasons for “serious breaches” of financial regulations by continental governing body UEFA. The ban was later overturned by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), which also reduced the accompanying $34 million fine to $11.3 million, ruling that City had failed to cooperate with UEFA.

But the result of this latest case with the Premier League could seriously damage the club going forward.

Possible punishments

According to the official league handbook, potential punishments could include a hefty points deduction, an unlimited fine, or even expulsion from the league entirely.

A case of this size has no precedent. Yes, clubs have fallen foul of slightly breaking Premier League rules in the past and have received points deductions as a result.

But as former England international and current pundit Ian Wright says, this is “cheating on an industrial scale.”

“It’s quite surreal seeing it written down like that,” he said on ITV. “I feel unprecedented punishment is required here.”

That punishment could be unlimited. That points deduction, for example, could be so big that it essentially relegates City into the Championship – the second tier of English soccer – or, as has been suggested by English media and pundits, spread out over multiple years to severely hamstring the club’s efforts to qualify for anything notable for the foreseeable future.

City’s triumphs after the period which covers the charges are tainted by the specter of what the independent commission called a “sham.” Michael Regan/Getty Images

There has also been talk that the club should be stripped of all the titles and trophies it won during the period in question. And while that makes sense on the surface, it also opens up another can of worms.

If City has its three league titles taken away from it, what happens to the teams that finished second that year? If those runners-up are awarded the league title, do they then deserve the prize money that would have come with it?

Also, what happens to all the teams that dropped points to City during those nine years? City’s results would have contributed to teams being relegated from the top division, or missing out on lucrative Champions League places. Could there be a scenario where every club during that period seeks compensation through legal actions for lost earnings and revenue? That process would surely take years.

And while this is a logistical headache for people in suits and boardrooms, the length of this case continues to undermine what’s happening on the pitch.

Already, despite the upcoming appeal, that nine-year period of the league now comes with an asterisk. All those titles won, goals scored and memories made have been cast in shadow for the players and fans who lived them.

“(City) knew it would hurt a lot of people, but they still done it,” former Manchester United and Ireland star and current pundit Roy Keane told ITV. “If I was a player, I would 100% be sticking those medals in the bin. It’s cheating.”

It’s a similar sentiment felt by former Liverpool player Jamie Carragher who told Sky Sports that he’d be “furious” if he was a City player from that time.

“I actually feel for the Man City players. I mean, as a team, what they’ve done is wrong. The Premier League have called it a sham five times in this statement.

“In terms of individual players, some of them were coming out to bat for the club and, you know as they would, that’s normal right now, and it must be very difficult for them to see what’s going on right now.

What’s next?

All of this has also been incredibly damaging for the Premier League’s reputation.

Ultimately, the ideal situation for the league would have been City being found innocent because things could have returned back to normal relatively quickly – even if opposition fans would have objected. It’s telling, then, that the league’s statement is so strong. It suggests just how much cheating and blatant disregard for the rules it thinks has gone on behind closed doors.

The punishment to be handed down by the independent commission will be decided sometime in the future. Mike Morese/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty Images

What happens next is unclear. City will appeal, we know that, and the Premier League is keen to close this matter as soon as possible and decide on a punishment fitting for the charges.

But the longer City digs its heels in, the more damaging this will get for everyone involved.

The club shows no signs of backing down, though, with CEO Ferran Soriano calling the case a “Premier League conspiracy theory” in an internal video sent to club staff after the verdict was announced.

Without knowing the outcome or City’s possible punishment – which the league has said will come at a later date by the independent commission – the pure essence of the Premier League is lost. If all of City’s results are to be scrapped this season, next season, or in four seasons to come, then whatever happens in the meantime is somewhat meaningless. The all-or-nothing nature of sports gets muddled with asterisks and different permutations.

It’s a sad state of affairs that could genuinely take weeks, months or even years to conclude, given City is showing no signs of backing down and can afford, ironically, the best legal team in the world.

Manchester City will next play on October 11 against Liverpool – one of the teams that missed out on winning a league title during the period of the charges.

Current City manager Enzo Maresca will have to try focus his plethora of star players – such as striker Erling Haaland – after what must have been a turbulent week for everyone involved at the club.

All of a sudden, their futures are very uncertain.

World.title: What have we learned about Pope Leo during his visit to France
World.content:
Metz, France — France may have a highly secularized culture, but it has given France may have a highly secularized culture, but it has given Pope Leo XIV a superstar welcome.

In Paris, around 800,000 lined the Champs-Élysées avenue, some waving Vatican or French flags while others climbed trees or stood on each other’s shoulders to get a glimpse of the popemobile.

In Lourdes, a holy site in southern France, around 150,000 attended an open-air papal Mass, according to Vatican estimates which dwarf the numbers of faithful who turned out for the last papal visit in 2008.

During the four-day visit, Leo appeared comfortable and relaxed, delivering most of his speeches and reflections in French, as the Chicago-born pontiff sought to tackle several themes during the trip.

A strong focus of Leo’s has been on trying to revitalize faith in a traditional European Catholic heartland as well as on addressing the clerical sexual abuse scandal and big political topics such as artificial intelligence. He’s also offered some more personal, unscripted remarks, helping to shape a clearer picture of himself.

He wants Europe to draw on its Christian roots

While his predecessor never made official visits to the major Catholic European countries of France and Spain, Pope Leo has traveled to both within the first year and a half since his election.

France is sometimes described as the “eldest daughter of the church” because of its deep Catholic roots, but it’s also faced a long-term trend of declining church attendance with estimates of just 5-8% of the population heading to the pews each week.

French bishops have more recently reported some good news though: a surprising rise in new church entrants after around 8,200 adolescents and 13,200 adults were baptized in 2026. That’s a 20% increase on the year prior, with the church also saying 42% of the adults seeking baptism are aged 18-25, a reflection of a trend showing Gen Z’s openness to religious faith.

It’s something Pope Leo will have noted at the Stade de France when 80,000 young people packed the venue for a jubilant – and loud – prayer vigil. It was similar to when the pontiff visited Spain in June.

Pope Leo XIV on stage next to French bishop Etienne Guillet during a prayer vigil with young people at the Stade de France on Friday. Aurore Marechal/Getty Images

“There is a quest for meaning. People need and are in search of meaning and answers to the big existential question,” Rev. Benoît Pouzin, a priest in southwest France involved in youth ministry, told CNN.

France has a strict separation between church and state, so each papal visit needs to be carefully navigated. But in a surprising twist, Leo’s Mass in Paris was celebrated on the Place de la Concorde, a site deeply linked to the secular Republic as it’s where the last king of France, Louis XVI and Marie-Antoinette were guillotined. The separation of the church started with the fall of the monarchy during the French Revolution.

In another unusual move later in the trip, President Emmanuel Macron also attended a papal Mass in Metz, a city in the northeast, despite criticism in 2023 for doing the same during Pope Francis’ visit.

Pope isn’t panicking over AI, but warns of its power

Many among the crowds also pointed to Leo’s role as the other major US leader on the world stage. It’s hard not to see him as a counterweight to President Donald Trump. In contrast to the Trump administration, the pope has called for stronger guardrails around the development of artificial intelligence, warning against a “paradise of machines” while in Paris.

Pope Leo said he is taking the warnings about Artificial Intelligence’s threat to humanity seriously, and said it is irresponsible for people to sit back and dismiss the risks of AI.

Trump has dismissed the warnings about AI as a “hoax” which he made during a surprise phone call with Jensen Huang, the CEO of chipmaker Nvidia, at a summit in Los Angeles.

“I don’t think that that is fake news – as some have said – to try and pause,” Leo XIV said on board the papal plane from Metz to Rome.

Leo, who has expressed a keen interest in artificial intelligence since the start of his papacy, said that he found it “interesting” that Huang had unveiled a new tool to prevent AI agents from operating out of human control.

“He’s the same one, however, that says there should be no limits placed and no government regulation,” the Pope said.

The pope devoted his first major theological document to AI earlier this year, warning about the use of AI in warfare and calling for stronger ethical foundation to the development of the technology.

The pope explained that the Vatican had established its own AI commission to understand how to use it, along with the risks and benefits, and that “we need to continue to invite political leaders, the leaders of AI” so they can “look at what is happening already and what could be down the road.”

He explained: “We are trying to continue to promote dialog, study, investigation, to find ways to make sure that AI does not get to a point where it could destroy humanity.”

“If someone were to ask me, am I in panic mode? No, I’m not, I sleep at night” the pope said, but added: “I do think that the concerns raised by many of the experts, specialists in AI, should be taken seriously.”

“To simply say, oh, it’s not going to happen and close our eyes to it, I think, is probably not the most responsible way to go about that,” Leo said.

Concern over the far right and Christianity

The pope, who spoke out against the US war in Iran, also wants a more united Europe, a stronger European Union and stronger international cooperation. “Today, relations between individuals and states are becoming increasingly uncivilized,” the pope said in Metz on Monday. “The value of keeping one’s word is dismissed; instead, people boast of lies and deceit.”

The pope’s speech also praised one of the founders of the European Union, Robert Schuman, for whom there is an ongoing formal cause to make a saint.

Pope Leo XIV has warned against the use of Christianity by far-right political groups, while calling on the church to be active in seeking to prevent extremism. Speaking on board the papal plane, he said that “the combination of these far-right points of view with a certain kind of religion” cannot be considered an “authentic expression of Christianity.”

The pope’s comments came in response to a question about the rise of extremist parties in Germany as he flew back from making a major speech on European Unity at the French-German border.

“We go back to the values of the Gospel [Christian teaching], which are not about hatred and division, but they’re about understanding and compassion,” the pope said.

Pope Leo XIV delivers a speech during a meeting at the Robert Schuman Conference Center in Metz on Monday. Benoit Tessier/AFP/Getty Images

The American pontiff also responded to Trump’s White House media ban, which includes CNN and other outlets. In answer to a question from CNN, he said he was “very happy that, here, you are all welcome and good coverage, I think, is very important and that we have it all the way around, for everyone.” The response was classic Leo: signaling his support for the press but not wishing to create an unnecessary dispute with the president.

The American pope’s in-flight interactions with journalists were rare, unscripted moments, with his answers often revealing more about his personality. On the flight from Rome to Paris, the pope was asked if he had anything to do with a miraculous recent Chicago White Sox victory, his beloved baseball team. “No comment,” he said before adding with a smile, “Great things happen in Chicago.”

He also recalled childhood memories of watching Fulton Sheen, the American archbishop and broadcaster who was recently declared “blessed,” one step ahead of sainthood, and revealed he’d been practicing his French but was no longer using the Duolingo language app. “It’s fake news!” he said about recent reports. Leo has in the past been spotted using Duolingo to learn German.

Leo isn’t simply vocal about challenges of his homeland. He also voiced concern over assisted dying with France recently approving legislation granting the right to the incurably ill, which is strongly opposed by the Catholic Church. Leo spoke on the subject several times during his visit – most clearly in the “miracle shrine” town of Lourdes, known for drawing many sick and terminally ill pilgrims to its shrine.

A willingness to tackle church scandal

Workers are fitting the fixings that will hold in place the tarpaulins covering allegedly abusive priest Marko Rupnik’s mosaics on the façade of the Basilica of the Rosary ahead of Pope Leo XIV s visit to the shrine at Lourdes. Jean-Christophe Chartre/Hans Lucas/AFP/Getty Images

The pope must, however, continue to wrestle with Catholic Church’s sexual abuse scandals. France was left shocked by a 2021 report that estimated around 330,000 children were sexually abused over 70 years by priests or other church figures. He addressed this by telling crowds the church must admit its own failings and heal “deep wounds” before holding a two-hour meeting with seven survivors of abuse.

The Vatican said that Leo thanked them “for their painful testimony” while “reaffirming his commitment to ensuring that the harm they suffered is not repeated for others.”

But the scandal still lingers. On the façade of the basilica in Lourdes, banners were placed over controversial mosaics ahead of Leo’s visit. These mosaics – which will now be covered indefinitely – were designed by a Slovenian priest and artist, Rev. Marko Rupnik, accused of sexual and psychological abuse of adult women. A local bishop said the pope backed how the apostolic nunciature was handling the artist’s works. Bishop Jean-Marc Micas also said Leo had ordered the Vatican’s in-house media outlets to stop using Rupnik art. Rupnik, who maintains his innocence, is facing a church trial in the Vatican, which complainants say is taking too long and lacks transparency.

The pope was elected 16-months ago and is still carving out a narrative for his papacy. Some in the Vatican find him difficult to read, and the pope is known for keeping his cards close to his chest. But it’s out on the open road when he travels abroad, in France and, in November, in Latin America, where the Leo papacy is beginning to take shape.

World.title: FAZ Kopala holds  workshop for referee trainers
World.content:
The Football Association of Zambia (FAZ) Copperbelt Referees Desk has held a capacity building workshop in Kitwe for referees training officers from eight districts of the province as the 2026 transitional season kicks off.

Referees training officers from Kitwe, Ndola, Mpongwe, Chingola, Chililabombwe, Kamfinsa, Chambishi and Kalulushi were in attendance.

Former National Referees Manager Dr Derick Kafuli was the facilitator at the training workshop in Kitwe on Friday.

Dr Kafuli, the former FIFA-accredited referee, said well-trained referees are essential to the promotion of football.

“It was a very successful and important training. I believe well-trained referees are the beginning of good football. We have equipped training officers who are going to train our referees for the betterment of our football,” Dr Kafuli said.

FAZ Copperbelt Referees Manager Evans Malata hailed the training workshop for referees training officers.

“We wanted to equip our referees training officers from all our districts on the Copperbelt Province. The seminar was very successful and very okay because we had experts in refereeing like Dr Derick Kafuli and Mr Bernard Chabala as facilitators,” Malata said.

“We are talking about experienced referees coaches and assessors whom we are depending on regarding the growth of refereeing,” he said.

Malata declared referees on the Copperbelt ready for the transitional season.

“Our referees are ready to handle matches as you know some are even handling Africa Cup qualifiers and CAF club games. Our referees are ready for the challenge ahead,” said Malata, the retired referee himself.

Malata has in the recent past advocated for capacity building among referees as a way of growing Zambian football.

World.title: President Hichilema reaffirms Zambia-UK historic partnership
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has reaffirmed Zambia’s long-standing ties with the United Kingdom, describing the partnership as rooted in years of mutual trust, investment and shared values.

Speaking when His Majesty’s Trade Commissioner for Africa, Alastair Long, paid a courtesy call on him at State House, President Hichilema said he was delighted to receive the Commissioner, describing his visit as important to Zambia and to the continued strengthening of bilateral ties.

President Hichilema said Zambia values the long-standing cooperation with the United Kingdom, noting that British investments in the country have left a lasting legacy.

He said for many years, Zambia was not fully utilising the potential of that partnership, but his administration has now begun to do so.

The President noted that the younger generation of Zambians is becoming increasingly conscious that electricity and energy security is critical to national development, an area where Zambia has potential to be a leading producer.

“And the younger generation of Zambians might be a little bit conscious that electricity is very important and I suspect that you’re one of the leading producers of energy, family energy,” he said.

President Hichilema traced part of his own journey to Commonwealth development cooperation, recalling his early years after undergraduate studies, and said Zambia respects and values the relationship with the UK.

“So we do respect and value this relationship. So we’re very grateful,” he said.

He expressed gratitude to the UK for its continued support and asked Commissioner Long to continue the journey of deepening trade and investment cooperation.

Meanwhile, United Kingdom Trade Commissioner for Africa, Alastair Long, who recently assumed office, said the United Kingdom is committed to investing and contributing to Zambia’s “Grow Zambia Agenda” being spearheaded by President Hichilema.

Mr Long, who previously served as Deputy Trade Commissioner and later Trade Commissioner for Africa between 2019 and 2022 before serving as His Majesty’s Ambassador to Bahrain, said Zambia has taken significant steps to stabilise the economy and prepare for a bright future.

“The UK is really proud of our relationship, we are also incredibly proud of the investment relationship and Zambia has great potential to grow with the coming of the Grow Zambia Agenda,” Mr Long said.

World.title: President Hichilema calls on Parliamentarians to support Grow Zambia Agenda
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has called on all parliamentarians to support the Grow Zambia Agenda for creation of jobs, opportunities for citizens and to improve the lives of Zambians.

President Hichilema says that Parliament should enact laws that advance the grow Zambia Agenda in order to move forward as a nation

And the President indicated that his government will continue with various reforms across different sectors including in energy, mining and education, noting that reforms have delivered positively for the country.

Speaking during the Presidential approbation ceremony for the re-elected Speaker of the National Assembly Nelly Mutti and her two deputies, Malungo Chisangano and Nshamba Muzungu at State House, the Head of state said patriotism should shape both deliberations and conduct of the house as laws enacted will reflect on the development of the country.

The Head of State implored the three presiding leaders of the National assembly to effectively guide the house by ensuring that every voice is heard and national interest takes precedence.

He noted that national diversity is the strength of the country, as every value extracted from all parts of Zambia should be cherished.

President Hichilema clearly indicated that no law maker is second to none and that everyone should be treated equally regardless of the political party to which they were voted in.

He charged that there should be constructive cooperation among MPs, or that the House risks slowing down business and national development.

And he said that Parliament must unite the people through factual and respectful debates, while also calling for fair representation.

“To you Madam Speaker of the National Assembly, through your guidance in the house must embed the one Zambia, one nation and one people motto consciously. We have various political parties with one shared responsibility to advance the interest of the people,” President Hichilema stated.

Congratulating the trio, He noted that their selection to preside over the affairs of the National Assembly carries the trust of the House and is a reflection of the confidence in their ability to provide leadership and firm direction.

The President added that the election process at Parliament earlier today will remain historic because of the diverse composition of the MPs that elected the trio, including 20 women, 15 young people and five persons living with disabilities selected under the mixed member proportional representation.

He attributed the development to the constitutional reforms through the enactment of bill 10, describing it as a revolutionary decision.

“I have no doubt that the composition reflects the will and a clear endorsement from the Zambian people,” he added.

Meanwhile, Dr Mutti described her re-election as speaker which went unopposed as a privilege, noting that it shows that the House still has confidence in her leadership.

She pledged to ensure the dignity, honor and decorum of the House is maintained through reasonable debates, supported by facts.

She further assured the protection of new members who should not be obstructed or intimidated by senior members.

“The 14th National Assembly has come at a good time when the policy of the government is to Grow Zambia, and in whatever we do as a house our deliberations will be channeled towards that,” Mrs Mutti stated.

World.title: Transitional season kicks off as Power face Konkola
World.content:
The 2026 transitional Super Division campaign will kick off on Saturday, 3rd October, with defending champions Power Dynamos facing Konkola Blades in a seemingly unpredictable fixture at Konkola Stadium in Chililabombwe.

It was at Konkola Stadium where Power were confirmed league winners last season after edging Blades 2-1 in May.

Power and Konkola will face off in one of the five Stream A matches.

Power coach Oswald Mutapa said the Arthur Davies side must show the character of champions.

“It is important that we start on a positive note. We are champions so we have to show why we are champions,” Mutapa said in a pre-match comment.

“It won’t be an easy game, Konkola Stadium is a very difficult ground to go to but I feel we should be able to get the result,” he said.

Konkola coach Beston Chambeshi is pleased with his team’s preparedness for the new campaign.

“I think the team is ready for the season. The team is intact,” Chambeshi said.

“It is good we are starting with a team of Power’s calibre. We are playing in the same league with Power. Playing champions gives morale and confidence to our players,” he said.

Meanwhile, Power’s Kitwe rivals Nkana will tackle promoted side Trident away at Sentinel Ground.

Trident coach Kebby Hachipuka has declared that his team does not fear Nkana, the 13-time top league kings.

“Nkana is one of the biggest teams in Zambia, but we are not scared of them. We give them respect but we cannot be intimidated,” Hachipuka said.

Nkana coach Elijah Tana is seeking a positive start to the new campaign.

“The preparations went on well. Players have been putting in 100 percent in training,” Tana said.

“It is not an easy game but we have planned for it,” he said.

World.title: Zambia Futsal Team heads to Egypt for Pre-AFCON Camp
World.content:
Zambia National Futsal Team Head Coach, Andrea Cristoforetti, says the team is physically fit and ready to compete as it departs for Egypt for a pre-Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) training camp.

Speaking before departure today, Cristoforetti says the team had completed weeks of intensive preparations, covering key aspects needed ahead of the continental competition.

He said the team was aware of the challenges posed by its opponents, particularly the experienced North African sides.

Cristoforetti said the planned matches against Egypt, ranked among Africa’s leading futsal teams, would provide a crucial test of Zambia’s readiness.

Cristoforetti said the players had maintained good physical condition, with no injury concerns reported ahead of departure.

He said the technical bench and players were committed to giving their best, adding that the team was eager to participate in the competition.

Cristoforetti noted that qualifying for the AFCON for the second consecutive time, was already a significant achievement, as Zambia is among the eight best futsal teams on the continent.

He said the team is now focused on making further progress in the tournament, adding that selecting the final squad had been difficult because of the increased depth of talent and commitment demonstrated by players during previous training camps.

Cristoforetti said the players selected had a responsibility to represent the country and deliver results, while also honouring the efforts of those who were not included in the final squad.

World.title: DAPP Zambia celebrates 40-years anniversary
World.content:
Ministry of Community Development and Social Services Permanent Secretary, Angela Kawandami has commended Development Aid from People to People (DAPP) Zambia for its 40-year contribution to national development.

Ms Kawandami says DAPP Zambia’s work in education, health, agriculture, livelihoods, youth empowerment and community development had complemented Government’s efforts to improve the wellbeing of communities.

The Permanent Secretary was speaking when she officiated at the DAPP Zambia 40th anniversary celebration held at the National Partnership Office in Lusaka today.

Ms Kawandami said the organisation’s Farmers Clubs approach, which promotes knowledge sharing, climate-smart agriculture, sustainable land management and savings initiatives, supports the Grow Zambia Agenda aimed at increasing production, expanding economic opportunities and creating jobs.

She said sustainable development required partnerships among Government, communities, the private sector, development partners, civil society and other stakeholders.

Ms Kawandami also recognised DAPP Zambia’s contribution to education through teacher training and vocational skills development, as well as its work in health, including HIV, tuberculosis, malaria and community health programmes.

She further highlighted the organisation’s support to children and young people through initiatives such as Children’s Town, the Youth Academy and Youth in Action.

Ms Kawandami said Government remained committed to creating an enabling environment for civil society organisations and development partners to contribute to national development.

“Together, we can build stronger and more resilient communities,” she said.

Speaking at the same event, DAPP Zambia Managing Director, Elise Soerensen, said the organisation’s 40-year journey in Zambia has been anchored on working with communities to create sustainable development.

Ms Soerensen said DAPP Zambia had, since its establishment in 1986, worked with Government, development partners and communities in areas including agriculture, health, education, youth development and environmental protection.

She explained that DAPP Zambia started its work by supporting youth capacity building through Zambia National Service camps before expanding into tree planting, agriculture and environmental protection.

Ms Soerensen said the organisation had also established programmes such as Children’s Town and the Youth Academy to provide education, vocational skills and opportunities for vulnerable young people.

She said DAPP’s health interventions had evolved over the years to address HIV, tuberculosis, malaria, immunisation and other community health needs.

Ms Soerensen added that DAPP’s HIV programming alone covered more than 1,400 health facilities across Zambia by 2025.

She expressed gratitude to Government, development partners, private sector partners, traditional leaders, communities, staff and volunteers for contributing to DAPP Zambia’s achievements over the past 40 years.

“People are the drivers of their own development,” she said.

She reaffirmed DAPP Zambia’s commitment to working with communities to create opportunities and address emerging development challenges.

Meanwhile, a beneficiary of DAPP Zambia, Juliet Sakala, has shared how the organisation transformed her life after she tested HIV positive in 2002.

Ms Sakala, who described herself as a child of DAPP, said her journey began in Kalomo when she joined the organisation as a peer educator after losing her job as a volunteer with a water and sewerage company.

She said the training she received through DAPP equipped her with knowledge on HIV prevention, testing and community education, which encouraged her to privately undergo an HIV test.

Ms Sakala said the result was positive, a development she initially struggled to accept and feared sharing with others.

“DAPP empowered me with knowledge and skills that helped me overcome stigma and support others in my community,” she said

She said her experience with DAPP demonstrated the importance of empowering people with knowledge and skills that enable them to support others in their communities.

Ms Sakala said she is now doing well and continues to draw inspiration from the training and opportunities she received through DAPP.

World.title: DRMD finalises El Nino Preparedness Action Plan
World.content:
The Disaster Risk Management Division (DRMD) under the Office of the Vice President, with support from stakeholders comprising Government Line Ministries, the United Nations System, and Non-Governmental and Civil Society Organisations, has finalised the 2026/2027 El Niho Cluster Readiness, Preparedness and Anticipatory Action Plan.

This is a multi-sectoral plan to guide the country’s preparedness and early action ahead of the anticipated El Niño-influenced 2026/2027 rainfall season.

The plan is in response to the 2026/2027 seasonal rainfall forecast indicating a likelihood of below-normal rainfall in the Southern part of the country and above-normal rainfall in the Northern half part of the country.

DRMD National Coordinator, Norman Chipakupaku has highlighted that prolonged dry spells are also expected in some areas during critical periods of the agricultural season, requiring early preparedness for multiple and interconnected hazards.

Mr Chipakupaku noted that the plan focuses on strengthening early warning and early action, pre-positioning essential supplies, protecting vulnerable groups and maintaining critical services.

He added that it will strengthen food and water security, support continuity of learning and enhance risk communication and community engagement.

Mr Chipakupaku further explained that the plan will on the other hand bring preparedness and anticipatory actions in key sectors, including agriculture, food security and livestock, health, education, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene, energy, protection and emergency logistics.

He reiterated that the plan provides for risk communication and community engagement to ensure that communities are better prepared for possible impacts of the 2026/2027 rainfall season.

Mr Chipkupaku stated that the plan had been developed in line with the Disaster Management Amendment Act Number 2 of 2026, read together with the DMMU Act Number 13 of 2010, which mandates the institution to coordinate disaster management and formulate preparedness strategies and action plans.

He has since called on government institutions, the United Nations system, cooperating partners, humanitarian organisations, faith-based organisations, civil society, the private sector, traditional leaders, local authorities and communities to work together in implementing the plan.

Mr Chipakupaku further urged stakeholders to align their interventions, share information and resources, and strengthen coordination at all levels to avoid duplication of efforts and ensure the efficient use of available resources.

World.title: Nigeria: Boko Haram Fighters Gun Down Farmers in Borno
World.content:
Suspected Boko Haram insurgents have ambushed and killed 15 farmers, while abducting three others in Marte Local Government Area of Borno State.

According to local sources, the tragic incident took place across the Ala, Gumna, and Musune wards near the headquarters of the area council, on Wednesday.

While initial reports of the attack reached the community on Wednesday evening, the task of recovering the bodies could not be completed until Thursday morning.

Recounting the borrowing aftermath of the assault, an anonymous source said, "Five bodies were initially recovered from the field, while others were found later. Three persons are still missing, and sources indicate they were abducted by the insurgents."

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The Public Relations Officer, Borno State Police Command, DSP Kenneth Nahum Daso, confirmed that 15 people lost their lives and confirmed that authorities were actively investigating the situation.

"We are making efforts to determine the whereabouts of the three people still missing," Daso said.

A grieving relative, whose cousin was among the victims, shared details of the execution-style killings.

She explained that the victims had gone to their farms to harvest crops when they were ambushed.

"They were forced to lie down and were shot in the head at close range. It was a gory sight," she said.

According to the relative, local community members bravely mobilized to scour the fields, retrieve the bodies, and ensure they were buried according to Islamic rites.

The massacre has drawn widespread outrage, with the human rights organization Amnesty International strongly condemning the violence as a horrific violation of international humanitarian law.

In a statement released on Friday, the organization expressed deep concern over the escalating violence against vulnerable populations in Northeast Nigeria.

"Amnesty International strongly condemns the horrific killing of at least 15 people in Marte Local Government Area of Borno State," the statement read. "The victims, who were local residents venturing into the surrounding areas to earn a living or harvest their crops, were ambushed and targeted by a suspected Boko Haram group."

The rights group emphasized that the deliberate targeting of civilians by non-state armed groups constitutes a war crime.

"Amnesty International calls on the Nigerian authorities to take immediate, transparent, and human-rights-compliant measures to protect vulnerable communities living in the region," the statement concluded.

Despite ongoing military operations in Nigeria's Northeast, farming communities continue to face severe security threats as insurgents frequently target agricultural workers in remote areas

World.title: Somalia: Somaliland Detains Austrian Over Spiny-Tailed Lizard Smuggling
World.content:
Hargeisa — Somaliland police and the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change have detained an Austrian national in the port city of Berbera after he was allegedly caught attempting to purchase and collect spiny-tailed lizards, locally known as caasho-badhi.

The Ministry of Environment said the man was apprehended in a joint operation with police in the Sahil region.

"The Ministry of Environment, in cooperation with the police, arrested an Austrian national in Berbera who was collecting spiny-tailed lizards, locally known as caasho-badhi," the ministry said.

Authorities said the animals were allegedly being collected with the intention of taking them to Europe. Officials displayed containers and other equipment they said were connected to the case.

The ministry did not identify the Austrian national or specify how many lizards had been recovered. It also did not immediately say whether formal charges had been filed.

Spiny-tailed lizards, commonly known as Uromastyx, are reptiles distinguished by their thick, heavily spiked tails and are found in arid regions of Africa and the Middle East.

The case has raised concerns about the collection of Somaliland's wildlife for the international exotic-pet trade, in which reptiles and other wild animals can be captured and sold abroad.

The Somaliland government warned residents against illegally capturing, selling or trafficking wildlife and urged the public to report suspicious activities to the Environment Ministry or security authorities.

(Reporting by HornDiplomat News Desk)

World.title: Ethiopia: AU Urges Restraint As Ethiopia, Eritrea, Egypt Tensions Rise
World.content:
Addis Ababa — The African Union Commission has urged Ethiopia, Eritrea and Egypt to exercise maximum restraint amid heightened tensions between the three countries, warning against actions or statements that could further destabilise the region.

In a statement issued in Addis Ababa on Oct. 1, the commission said it was closely following the situation with concern and called on the three African Union member states to avoid further escalation.

"The Commission calls on all three Member States to exercise maximum restraint and refrain from actions or statements that could further escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability," the statement said.

The AU Commission also stressed the importance of maintaining channels of communication between Addis Ababa, Asmara and Cairo as tensions have increased across the Horn of Africa.

It urged the three governments to address their differences through established diplomatic channels and peaceful dialogue, in accordance with the principles of the Constitutive Act of the African Union.

"The Commission further underscores the importance of preserving channels of communication and urges the three countries to address their differences through established diplomatic channels and peaceful dialogue," it said.

The commission said it was prepared to assist the three countries in efforts to reduce tensions and resolve their differences peacefully.

"The AU Commission stands ready, in consultation with the countries concerned, to support efforts towards de-escalation, dialogue and the peaceful resolution of differences," the statement said.

Reporting by HornDiplomat News Desk)

World.title: Uganda: Mountain Gorilla Population Rises to 1,063 Amid Calls to End Illegal Tracking
World.content:
The population of mountain gorillas in Uganda, Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo has risen to 1,063, up from about 300 in 1990, conservation officials have announced.

Of these, 459 are found in Uganda's Bwindi Impenetrable National Park, while the others live in Rwanda's Volcanoes National Park and the Democratic Republic of Congo's Virunga National Park.

The figures were revealed during Uganda's national World Gorilla Day celebrations held at Ruhija Community Playground in Rubanda District. World Gorilla Day is marked globally every September 24 to promote gorilla conservation.

This year's celebrations, hosted under the theme "Securing the Future: Restoring Indigenous Trees, Healthy Gorillas and Resilient Communities," brought together conservationists, government officials, local leaders and communities.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Uganda rotates the national World Gorilla Day event among Rubanda, Kisoro and Kanungu districts.

Officials attributed the increase in the gorilla population to habitat protection, regular monitoring, law enforcement and greater involvement of communities living near protected areas.

Ruhija Town Council Mayor Geoffrey Tumuhimbise commended communities around Bwindi for embracing conservation and urged the Uganda Wildlife Authority (UWA) to increase support to residents so they can benefit tangibly from protecting wildlife.

"Conservation should not only focus on protecting wildlife, but should also consider the welfare and livelihoods of communities living alongside protected areas," Tumuhimbise said.

Representing the Minister of Tourism, Wildlife and Antiquities, Commissioner John Magambo, Tom Butiime welcomed the increase but warned against illegal gorilla tracking in Kigezi, saying it undermines conservation and tourism.

"Gorillas are a key tourism asset that boosts national revenue and community incomes. Tracking must follow established guidelines. Some conservation partners use their positions to facilitate irregular tracking," Butiime noted.

Graffam said the discovery was particularly unusual for the small airport, where officers typically encounter prohibited items such as knives and oversized liquids.

World.title: FBI's first cyber fugitive on Ten Most Wanted list returns to US after capture in Venezuela
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A Venezuelan alleged Tren de Aragua leader who became the FBI's first-ever cyber fugitive on its Ten Most Wanted list is back on U.S. soil after being captured overseas last month.

Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre, 50, also known as "Prometheus" and "The Engineer," appeared in a Nebraska courtroom Friday to face charges tied to a multimillion-dollar ATM "jackpotting" scheme.

He pleaded not guilty to four federal conspiracy charges during his initial court appearance and will remain detained in Nebraska while awaiting trial, according to the Department of Justice (DOJ).

FBI Director Kash Patel touted Aguirre's return as the 10th Ten Most Wanted fugitive captured since the beginning of the Trump administration and the first cyber fugitive ever placed on the list.

KASH PATEL DEFENDS FBI'S ‘MOST WANTED’ BUSTS AMID MANIPULATION ACCUSATIONS, HIGHLIGHTS 'SUMMER HEAT' SUCCESS

"Now he’s back in the United States to face justice," Patel said. "This FBI is running on supercharged horsepower — and there is nowhere on this planet criminals can hide."

Patel said the 10 captures are more than 2½ times the total recorded during the previous four years.

Aguirre was apprehended last month in Venezuela, and Patel subsequently told lawmakers the FBI had captured one of the nation's top fugitives.

The FBI previously told Fox News Digital that Aguirre led "a large international conspiracy to steal millions of dollars from financial institutions in support of the Tren de Aragua, through an ATM jackpotting scheme since at least 2024."

FBI STRIKES BACK AT HACKING GROUP WITH OVERSEAS ARREST OF ALLEGED LEADER

An ATM "jackpotting" attack is a type of cyberattack in which criminals exploit vulnerabilities in an ATM, including through the use of malware, to force the machine to dispense cash, according to the DOJ.

Prosecutors say Canelon Aguirre developed malicious software and was one of the leaders of the alleged ATM jackpotting conspiracy.

The DOJ says the broader ATM jackpotting conspiracy has been linked to Tren de Aragua, which the U.S. has designated as a foreign terrorist organization.

Attorney General Todd Blanche said DOJ has charged nearly 350 alleged TdA members and associates since the designation.

"The capture and arrest of Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre marks yet another success for the Homeland Security Task Force and Joint Task Force Vulcan," Blanche said.

"We will continue to break up narcoterrorist finance networks, prosecute violent criminals, and keep American neighborhoods safe."

Aguirre faces four conspiracy counts involving bank fraud, bank burglary and computer fraud, money laundering and providing material support to terrorists.

The bank fraud conspiracy charge carries the highest maximum penalty at 30 years in prison, according to DOJ.

World.title: Blue state councilman mocked after claiming self-driving cars are 'murdering' pets: 'Hide your cats'
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

One Minneapolis city council member prompted widespread mockery on social media after going to bat for "cat lovers," claiming Waymo cars are killing cats and urging officials to require humans in the self-driving vehicles.

"I will say cats have been killed and cats have been killed by these autonomous vehicles," Jason Chavez told fellow council members. "I have a cat. I don't want my cat getting killed because of these autonomous vehicles.

"So, to those cat lovers out there, just know that these Waymo vehicles, these autonomous vehicles have killed cats and that's unfair.

"I just watched a video sitting here from the dais, and it was really hard to watch. Literally, cats being murdered by these vehicles."

WAYMO DRIVERLESS CARS OVERRUN ATLANTA NEIGHBORHOOD, CIRCLING CUL-DE-SACS AND ALARMING FAMILIES WITH KIDS

The ordinance, which narrowly passed Thursday, would mandate a human operator and a special license for all autonomous vehicles. But its future remains uncertain.

Mayor Jacob Frey announced he plans to veto the proposal in a statement to multiple Minnesota outlets, saying it "doesn't make sense," and the city will continue its efforts to embrace "innovative technology," including transportation options. Despite acknowledging the safety concerns, Frey added he would not support a "backdoor ban" of the vehicles.

As Waymo vehicles with rooftop sensors and empty seats become a more common sight, supporters argue requiring a human operator would effectively ban autonomous taxi services and result in higher fares, while opponents insist the technology poses safety risks and takes away jobs.

Social media users were quick to pile on Chavez's remarks about the potential threat to cats, accusing him of blowing the issue out of proportion and shifting focus from more pressing priorities in Minneapolis.

"The Minneapolis City Council wants to require a human in driverless vehicles because cats are being 'murdered' by them," Townhall columnist Dustin Grage posted on X. "This guy's salary is $110,000/year, by the way."

Grage took more swipes at Chavez in separate X posts, writing, "They're calling it the cat genocide" and, "Hide your cats. The Waymos are coming."

It seems Tennessee’s athletic department has a very good reason to continue its "Happy Hour" promotion for the remainder of the 2026 football season.

Last weekend, as the Vols were preparing to host No. 1 Texas, it was announced that President Donald Trump would be making the trip to Knoxville for the top-15 SEC showdown inside Neyland Stadium.
