World.title: Lord Ashcroft: Conservatives have work to do to unseat Carney
World.content:
Article content

Whether this impression is fair or groundless, it exists (when I asked my 10,000 poll respondents to tap in the word or phrase they most associated with the Conservatives, they were as likely to write “Trump” as “Pierre”) and it could hardly be more damaging. Four years ago, my polling found that only a quarter of Canadians saw the U.S. as a threat. Today, only a quarter see their southern neighbour as an ally. Canadians are more likely to have an unfavourable view of Trump than of Vladimir Putin, and they think it’s more important to stand up to Washington than Beijing. Though Trump will be gone in fewer than 850 days, voters overwhelmingly think the U.S. relationship will matter at least as much in the next Canadian federal election as it does now. “Trump winning a second term proves we can’t trust them,” one Ontario voter told us. “Even if Pete Buttigieg or Kamala Harris is president in 2028, what’s going to stop President JD Vance doing the exact same thing in 2032?” In Canada, each party’s approach to the question will be a crucial test of its values, priorities and fitness for government.

World.title: Colombia’s top corporate lobbyist resigns over reported tensions with president
World.content:
The director of one of Colombia’s most powerful business associations, Bruce Mac Master of the ANDI, resigned amid tensions with President Abelardo de la Espriella.

In a letter to the ANDI, Mac Master said that “it is time for me to step down from my role as head of the National Association of Entrepreneurs of Colombia.”

According to the former ANDI boss, “unexpected and troubling circumstances” made working for the association “particularly complex” and ‘multiple pressures have affected its ability to act freely and carry out its functions autonomously.”

In recent weeks, unexpected and troubling circumstances have arisen that have made the Association’s operating environment particularly complex, with potential adverse effects on its members and staff. Multiple pressures have affected its ability to act freely and carry out its functions autonomously. In the face of these challenges, I have sought to act with firmness and prudence, always prioritizing institutional channels and placing the interests of the ANDI above any personal considerations, in an effort to resolve this situation. Bruce Mac Master

Mac Master’s resignation followed news suggesting that De la Espriella instructed his cabinet of boycotting the ANDI chief.

According to political news magazine La Silla Vacia, the rift between the ANDI and the government was because De la Espriella’s law firm was never allowed to join the ANDI and the association’s donations in response to the august 10 earthquake bypassed the First Lady’s newly founded and very controversial foundation.

“The General Board of Directors, its Executive Committee, and I did everything in our power to facilitate a solution and create conditions that would allow the Association to fully fulfill its role, seeking to keep channels of dialogue open and to continue contributing,” but “all of those attempts were unsuccessful.”

I deeply regret this, because I have always believed in collective intelligence and in the need for the government, the private sector, and institutions to work together—even in the face of differences—with respect, independence, and a sense of national responsibility. We tried, but we were unsuccessful. Bruce Mac Master

Mac Master said that he hoped that his resignation would restore “collaboration between the national government and the business community—as represented by the General Board of Directors, the members, and the various divisions of the Association.”

The former ANDI chief had been trying to represent the business interests of its approximately 1,600 members since 2013.

World.title: Colombia seeks to tighten checks on public protests
World.content:
Colombia’s government published a draft decree that seeks to tighten regulations on public protests.

The draft was published weeks before labor unions and social organizations plan regional anti-government protests ahead of a national strike that is set for November.

The draft seeks to update the Decree #3 of 2021, which was issued months before a national strike that was violently repressed by the police and the military.

In an attempt to prevent another bloodbath, the decree seeks to regulate authorities’ response to protests and the coordinated use of force in response to acts of vandalism and violence.

The decree regulates dialogue between the protesters and law enforcement authorities to promote the peaceful nature of protests.

The decree additionally limits the use of police intelligence against those organizing and participating in the protests.

Last but not least, the decree seeks the effective prosecution of those arrested during protests through increased surveillance and a permanent police presence.

The decree comes amid social tensions that surged after the far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella took office in August and announced counterrevolutionary measures that seek to undo reforms by his leftist predecessor, former President Gustavo Petro.

Swelling student protests have been publicly accused of being fueled by insurgencies and De la Espriella has warned that police may enter universities if they find evidence they are used to prepare acts of vandalism or terrorism.

World.title: Colombia breaks diplomatic ties with Iran
World.content:
Colombia’s Foreign Ministry said Thursday that it had broken diplomatic ties with Iran and designated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization.

The foreign ministry made the announcements in two separate statements that were published in its website.

In the first statement, the government claimed that the decision claimed to defend “national and hemispheric security, and the fight against transnational crime.”

According to the foreign ministry, the Iranian government has “alleged ties to international terrorist groups and other narco-terrorist groups that threaten [Colombia’s] security.”

Colombia also took into account the documented human rights violations committed by the Iranian government on its territory, the verified attacks against countries not involved in the Middle East conflict, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and the authorities’ obstruction of the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) efforts to verify the scope of Iran’s nuclear program. Foreign Ministry

In regards to the IRGC, the foreign ministry claimed that the Iranian armed force “poses a serious threat to international peace and security” through “covert operations beyond Iran’s borders.”

“Colombia will strengthen its control and security measures to prevent individuals associated with the IRGC from entering its territory,” said the foreign ministry in a second statement.

In his 2017 book “Watch Your Backyard,” Foreign Minister Omar Bula claimed that “Iran and Islamic extremist groups such a Hezbollah and Al Qaeda have profusely penetrated Latin America.”

As part of his foreign policy, President Abelardo de la Espriella has renewed ties with the United States, Israel and the United Arab Emirates.

In a response, the Iranian government said that the accusations of the De la Espriella government go “against the principles of mutual respect” and damage both countries’ “interests and benefits.”

“It is clear that none of the arguments put forward by the Colombian government to justify this decision are valid or logical, and that this measure was adopted solely under the influence of the Zionist regime and the United States,” said Iran’s foreign ministry.

World.title: ACSN extends lockdown of Colombia’s Caribbean coast to Friday morning
World.content:
Santa Marta-based organized crime group ACSN said Wednesday that the lockdown it has imposed on parts of Colombia’s Caribbean coast will be lifted on Friday morning.

In its first formal statement, the ACSN said that “the armed strike announced for 72 hours will end at 7:00AM on Friday 25 September 2026.”

The lockdown, which was initially called for 48 hours on Monday, has devastated the legal economy in the port city, particularly after ACSN assassins uploaded videos of them opening fire at stores that ignored the order to social media.

The online videos and half a dozen burnt buses and taxis all but cleared the streets of Santa Marta, which became a ghost town on Tuesday.

“We have never seen anything like this,” one Santa Marta resident told news program El Reporte Coronell.

President Abelardo de la Espriella announced the militarization of Santa Marta, but this was barely visible in the city’s downtown area and in the majority of Santa Marta’s neighborhoods.

“There are no police or soldiers in the streets, the people feel unprotected and are in panic,” said journalist Javier Manjarres on social media platform X.

“The current situation is a consequence of the behavior of the security forces and the decisions taken by the National Government in regards to our organization,” the organized crime group said in their statement.

The ACSN admitted that the clandestine lockdown was the result of the killing of Jose Luis Perez, a.k.a. “Cholo,” one of its commanders in the region around the Sierra Nevada mountain range just outside the city.

According to the group, security forces executed Cholo in front of his wife after his arrest.

An 18-year-old farmhand with no ties to the organization was also executed by the security, his family told media.

The lockdown has been imposed throughout the Magdalena and La Guajira provinces, a region where the group dominates organized crime and controls drug trafficking route to the Caribbean.

World.title: Colombia withdraws support for ICJ genocide case against Israel
World.content:
Colombia has withdrawn its participation in South Africa’s genocide case against Israel, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) said Tuesday.

In a statement, the court in The Hague said that Colombia’s government “decided to withdraw the Declaration of intervention that it had filed… on 5 April 2024 in the case concerning Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide in the Gaza Strip.”

The decision of the administration of President Abelardo De la Espriella is part of a wider attempt to restore ties with Israel and its main sponsor, the United States, and appease its Evangelical Christian support base.

In response to the ongoing genocide in Palestine, former President Gustavo Petro took a leading role in diplomatic efforts that sought to isolate Israel and seek justice for Israel’s victims through the world court.

In a response, the US Government put Petro on a blacklist and actively campaigned for the election of De la Espriella to prevent another leftist victory in elections earlier this year.

The new president, who took office in August, immediately restored diplomatic ties to Israel and lifted a ban on coal exports to the country in West Asia.

World.title: ACSN crime group shuts down parts of Colombia’s Caribbean coast
World.content:
Santa Marta-based crime group ACSN shut down parts of the city and the surrounding region after Colombia’s armed forces killed one of their commanders.

Jose Luis Perez, a.k.a. “Cholo,” and six of his comrades were killed during an offensive on Monday.

The son of Fredy Castillo, a.k.a. “Pinocho,” who is one of the alleged bosses of the crime group, was reportedly among those killed during the operation.

Shortly after, a pamphlet that was signed by the ACSN ordered an “armed strike” of 48 hours because of the “the fierce attacks that the government has been launching against our organization in the Sierra Nevada since this afternoon.”

Multiple buses were incinerated in the region around Santa Marta.

We hereby declare a 48-hour armed strike throughout the province of Magdalena, particularly along the Troncal del Caribe highway, in the city of Santa Marta, and in the banana-growing region. We do not want any businesses to remain open for a period of 48 hours. ACSN

According to President Abelardo de la Espriella, who traveled to the city, “they are trying to intimidate the public by promoting an armed strike.”

“I will not allow any criminal organization to subjugate citizens through threats and terror,” the president added.

Notwithstanding, multiple shop owners in Santa Marta and along the highway kept their shops closed on Tuesday, afraid to challenge the authority of the local crime bosses.

The district government closed public schools in neighborhoods where the ACSN is believed to have a strong presence. Public transport was suspended as videos of armed men opening fire on shops that failed to close voluntarily were posted on social media.

The ACSN control much of drug trafficking to the port of Santa Marta and to the coastline of the neighboring La Guajira province.

De la Espriella ended attempts to negotiate the group’s surrender and ordered a military approach after taking office in August.

World.title: Colombia’s war crimes tribunal warns ICC that De la Espriella supports “worst attack in history”
World.content:
Colombia’s war crimes tribunal JEP said that it would warn the United Nations and the International Criminal Court about plans of President Abelardo de la Espriella to cut its budget.

In a statement, JEP president Alejandro Ramelli raised the alarm warned about a pending proposal by far-right Senator Enrique Gomez (National Salvation) to reduce the tribunal’s budget by COP100 billion ($31.6 million), which received De la Espriella’s support.

A second proposal by another far-right party, the Democratic Center, sought to push all sentences against members of the security forces to military justice for revision.

According to Ramelli, the two bill proposals “prove the existence of a strategy to block the JEP’s functioning” and called on the international community to “put a stop to this effort to dismantle our financial system and calls for the essential resources needed for our operations to be guaranteed.”

These initiatives constitute a combined strategy of economic strangulation and the subjugation of the JEP to military criminal justice. It is the most serious attack we have ever faced against our independence and autonomy. JEP president Alejandro Ramelli

The president , who vowed to get rid of the JEP on campaign, said that the 2027 national budget “does not constitute any threat to any judge, it’s the Constitution at work.”

I do not have a policy of retaliation against the JEP. I have a duty to manage spending, demand results, and allocate the State’s limited resources to a justice system that serves everyone, not to a court that part of the country perceives—for reasons debated in Congress and in public opinion—as a system of privileges rather than an effective end to impunity. President Abelardo de la Espriella

Since March of 2018, the JEP has played a key role in clarifying crimes committed during the armed conflict that erupted in response to the insurgency of the now-defunct guerrilla group FARC.

Among other things, the JEP found that the guerrillas recruited more than 18,000 children and that the security forces assassinated more than 7,800 civilians to inflate their combat kills.

Hundreds of former guerrillas and former members of the armed forces are taking part in a transitional justice system that seeks to solve as many as possible of the hundreds of thousands of crimes committed during the decades-long armed conflict.

World.title: Colombia pulls out of international LGBT coalition
World.content:
The government of President Abelardo de la Espriella pulled Colombia out of the international Equal Rights Coalition, which promotes the rights of sexual and gender minorities around the world.

The Foreign Ministry announced its departure from the coalition in a letter addressed to the organization of which Colombia was co-president until February next year.

According to Caribe Afirmativa, a gay rights NGO that was part of the international initiative, warned that the decision was “a serious setback in foreign policy and commitments to LGBTIQ+ rights.”

We also view this action as a snub to the international community, a break from the leadership role Colombia had established, and an unequivocal political signal regarding the place the current government is willing to grant to the rights of LGBTIQ+ people. Caribe Afirmativa

De la Espriella has appointed multiple prominent far-right figures in his government and has vowed to wage a “Culture War” against what it considers “gender ideology.”

On top of this, De la Espriella and multiple of his cabinet members oppose the right of gay couples to adopt children and reportedly sacked the newly appointed planning chief because he and his gay partner had adopted a child.

World.title: Brazil heads to the polls without a single debate between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro
World.content:
Brazil heads to the polls without a single debate between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro

2nd Friday, October 2026 - 07:53 UTC Full article

Globo said in a statement that “successive court decisions taken moments before the debate create legal uncertainty and represent undue interference in the media's freedom to organise debates”

Brazilian broadcaster Globo on Thursday cancelled, an hour before it was due to start, the last presidential debate scheduled before Sunday's first round, following a series of court rulings and the absence of both President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The two leading candidates thus head to the polls without having faced each other in a single televised debate during the entire campaign.

Lula had announced on Wednesday that he would not attend and would instead give an interview on the Flow podcast at the same time. At the request of his campaign, which cited a “potential imbalance”, Superior Electoral Court judge Estela Aranha barred the broadcaster from showing the president's empty lectern and from allowing other candidates to direct questions to it, two points included in the rules agreed with the contenders. The judge noted that attendance at debates is “optional”.

Following that ruling, Bolsonaro said he would not attend either. “I have just decided not to go to the Globo debate because of the censorship imposed on the event by the TSE. The press must be free and elections must be clean,” said the Liberal Party candidate. Supreme Federal Court justice Gilmar Mendes then ordered the inclusion of Renan Santos of the Missão party, who did not meet the requirement of having at least five members of Congress.

Globo said in a statement that “successive court decisions taken moments before the debate create legal uncertainty and represent undue interference in the media's freedom to organise debates”.

In the interview, Lula called the format “fruitless”, said it allowed “little jokes” from candidates with less support and proposed that debates be organised according to each candidate's electoral weight. “I like you better than Globo,” he told the host.

Thursday was also the last day of electoral advertising. Lula, who turns 81 on October 27, said: “This is my last election,” and pledged to shorten the working week to eliminate Saturday work. Bolsonaro called for leaving behind “the old system” and avoided direct attacks on the president. Polls show them in a statistical tie in a possible runoff.

World.title: A million square kilometres short: the ice ring around Antarctica keeps shrinking
World.content:
A million square kilometres short: the ice ring around Antarctica keeps shrinking

2nd Friday, October 2026 - 07:00 UTC Full article

Extent peaked on September 14 at 17.59 million square kilometres, more than a million below the historical average

The sea ice surrounding Antarctica reached its third-lowest winter maximum this year since satellite records began in 1979, according to the US National Snow and Ice Data Center. The four lowest maxima in the record have occurred in the last four years.

Extent peaked on September 14 at 17.59 million square kilometres, more than a million below the historical average. Only the winters of 2023 and 2024 recorded lower maxima. The centre took time to confirm the figure because Antarctic sea ice fluctuates considerably around its maximum; after that date, extent continued to decline.

Sea ice is frozen seawater that forms around the continent each winter and largely melts during the summer. Its retreat does not in itself raise sea levels, since it is already floating, but scientists track it as an indicator of the state of the Southern Ocean. With less ice, the ocean absorbs more heat and the ice shelves fringing the continent become more exposed to waves; those shelves act as a barrier slowing the flow of glaciers into the sea.

“After several decades of stable or increasing winter Antarctic sea ice conditions, it is concerning to see these low values persisting,” Lettie Roach, a climate scientist at Germany's Alfred Wegener Institute, told the specialist site Carbon Brief. According to Clare Eayrs of the Korea Polar Research Institute, July recorded the fifth-lowest extent on record and August the fourth-lowest, and all five of the lowest Julys have occurred since 2022. In the Bellingshausen Sea, the shortfall against the average reached about 650,000 square kilometres.

For Argentine glaciologist Lucas Ruiz, the records no longer represent an exception but a trend: very low anomalies have been observed since at least 2017, and winter extent has not exceeded the historical average since 2021. Diego Winocur, a researcher at the University of Buenos Aires, said the current El Niño may have played a role through changes in winds and storm tracks, though the specialists consulted agree it is not enough to fully explain the decline. Water temperature appears to be a decisive factor.

Until 2016, Antarctic sea ice had remained stable and even grown slightly, unlike in the Arctic. Scientists are still debating whether the decline of recent years marks a lasting shift.

World.title: British foreign secretary reiterates support for the Falklands in meeting with Cheryl Roberts
World.content:
British foreign secretary reiterates support for the Falklands in meeting with Cheryl Roberts

1st Thursday, October 2026 - 23:07 UTC Full article

Roberts holds the Trade, Industry and Mineral Resources portfolio in the archipelago's government and announced on September 21 the five-year extension of offshore hydrocarbon licences.

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband hosted Cheryl Roberts, a member of the Falkland Islands Legislative Assembly, in London on Thursday, and reiterated to her that the United Kingdom “stands shoulder to shoulder” with the archipelago's residents and “remains steadfast” in supporting their right “to determine their own future and develop their own resources”.

Miliband posted the message on X after the meeting, held at the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office. The Legislative Assembly said the foreign secretary had expressed London's “unwavering” support for the archipelago. Neither side gave details of the topics discussed.

Roberts holds the Trade, Industry and Mineral Resources portfolio in the archipelago's government and announced on September 21 the five-year extension of offshore hydrocarbon licences.

It is the foreign secretary's first meeting with an assembly member since Argentina announced arbitration against the United Kingdom over the Sea Lion oil project on September 28, giving London two weeks to halt exploitation. The “shoulder to shoulder” wording echoes the response issued on September 30 by Overseas Territories Minister Uma Kumaran.

Argentina claims sovereignty over the archipelago and maintains that licences granted by the local government are invalid. In the 2013 referendum, on a 92% turnout, 99.8% of voters chose to retain the status of a British overseas territory.

World.title: British-Iranian man arrested over the RAF Fairford incident
World.content:
British-Iranian man arrested over the RAF Fairford incident

1st Thursday, October 2026 - 22:26 UTC Full article

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said there were “strong indications” that Iran “played a part” in what happened, though he said he could not give details and that the investigation was ongoing

British counter-terrorism police on Thursday arrested a 25-year-old man with dual British and Iranian nationality in London on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts, in connection with Sunday's incident near RAF Fairford, an airbase in western England used by the United States Air Force.

The arrest took place in Westminster, where two properties were searched. Police had initially said the detained man was 27 and that a second man had been questioned, but corrected both points in a later update. The five men arrested near the base on Sunday — British nationals aged 23 to 25 who live in London — remain on police bail. None has been charged.

The five were detained in the early hours after reports of three suspicious vehicles heading towards the base, first on suspicion of explosives offences and later on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act. Petrol, but no explosive devices, was found in vans near the site. According to the BBC, one of them had himself dialled the emergency number an hour before a local resident reported a group of masked men.

“The investigation is hugely complex,” said Vicki Evans, senior national coordinator for counter-terrorism policing, adding that “all possible angles, including foreign state involvement” are being examined.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday there were “strong indications” that Iran “played a part” in what happened, though he said he could not give details and that the investigation was ongoing. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi replied that Burnham was “barking up the wrong tree”, and Tehran denied any involvement. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had spoken on Monday of “the hands of a foreign actor”, without providing evidence. Washington criticised the release on bail; Burnham defended it, citing the strict conditions imposed.

RAF Fairford has been used by the US Air Force for decades. In recent months, bombers have taken off from there for the Middle East after the British government approved its use for what it called defensive strikes on Iran.

World.title: Christa Pike survives a failed execution in Tennessee and remains in critical condition
World.content:
Christa Pike survives a failed execution in Tennessee and remains in critical condition

1st Thursday, October 2026 - 22:20 UTC Full article

Pike, 50, was given both doses of pentobarbital set out in the state protocol — two 50-millilitre syringes — at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville

Christa Pike, the only woman on death row in the US state of Tennessee, survived a lethal injection execution attempt on Wednesday and remains in critical condition in hospital, her lawyers said. Her defence has asked Governor Bill Lee to commute her sentence.

Pike, 50, was given both doses of pentobarbital set out in the state protocol — two 50-millilitre syringes — at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville. Witnesses said she was still breathing and could be heard snoring nearly an hour later, when they were escorted out of the room. She was taken by ambulance to a nearby hospital. “Christa is alive right now. We don't have a sense of her prognosis, but we do know that she is alive and receiving life-saving medical care,” Randy Spivey of the Tennessee Office of the Post-Conviction Defender said on Thursday.

The Department of Correction said “every step of the state's lawful and established execution protocol” approved by the Attorney General's office had been followed, but did not explain why the procedure was not completed or give details of her condition. The defence alleged difficult vein access, blown veins, degraded pentobarbital and a lack of emergency medical care, and criticised the secrecy of the protocol. Joel Zivot, a professor at Emory University's School of Medicine and an adviser to Pike's legal team, told the BBC the drug probably never reached a sufficient level in her blood and that she was likely to suffer brain injury.

Pike was convicted of the murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in Knoxville in January 1995, when she was 18. The victim's family has demanded answers following the failed procedure. Had it been completed, it would have been the first execution of a woman in Tennessee in more than two centuries.

The state adopted its single-drug protocol after a three-year pause: Governor Lee halted executions in 2022 when an investigation found prison officials had not followed their own drug-testing rules, and they resumed in 2025. In January of that year, then US Attorney General Merrick Garland withdrew the federal pentobarbital-based protocol, citing the risk of unnecessary pain and suffering. In January 2026, Pike sued the state, arguing that a blood disorder made the method unconstitutionally cruel in her case; a judge declined in August to block the execution.

According to the Death Penalty Information Center, seven of the twenty execution attempts carried out in the United States in 2022 had visible problems.

World.title: Punta Arenas and Falklands businesses hold more than 800 meetings
World.content:
Punta Arenas and Falklands businesses hold more than 800 meetings

1st Thursday, October 2026 - 21:33 UTC Full article

The event precedes a direct sea link using a Chilean-flagged vessel operated by Easter Island Naviera, which the company plans to launch between mid-November and the end of the year

Business people from Punta Arenas, in southern Chile, and from the Falklands held 822 business meetings over two days, at an event the organisers described as a success and which serves as a prelude to the reopening of a direct sea route between the Chilean city and Stanley, planned for the coming months.

The “Punta Arenas – The Islands Business Meeting” took place on Monday 28 and Tuesday 29 September at the Hotel Cabo de Hornos. It was organised by the Municipality of Punta Arenas and Chilean shipping company Easter Island Naviera, and brought together some 60 Magallanes companies and a delegation of 42 representatives from 32 companies and organisations in the archipelago, led by Louise Ellis, deputy managing director of the Falkland Islands Development Corporation. Sectors invited included food, cleaning products, cement, timber and spare parts. According to the organisers, several business people closed contracts, though no number was given.

“It has been a good couple of days; we are on a journey to connect the past with the future. We have worked with Punta Arenas and Magallanes for many decades. It was interrupted recently, but we hope to work again with old and new friends,” said Mike Summers, director of the Falkland Islands Chamber of Commerce and a former member of the Legislative Assembly. Ellis said there was interest on both sides in doing business.

The event precedes a direct sea link using a Chilean-flagged vessel operated by Easter Island Naviera, which the company plans to launch between mid-November and the end of the year. Its general manager, Pablo Pacheco, described it as a supply route “between private parties”. The mayor of Punta Arenas, Claudio Radonich, said the city aims to become the islands' “big supermarket”.

The Chilean government has called the initiative “a business between private parties”. Defence Minister Fernando Barros had said days earlier that Chile's support for Argentina's sovereignty claim does not imply restrictions on trade with the archipelago. According to the Chilean press, Argentina's foreign ministry followed the event closely; there was no official Argentine statement on it.

The new route would compete with supplies that currently reach the islands from Montevideo.

World.title: Uruguay's foreign minister separates the "invaded island" from the money extracted from the Falklands
World.content:
Uruguay's foreign minister separates the “invaded island” from the money extracted from the Falklands

1st Thursday, October 2026 - 09:32 UTC Full article

The minister said this was the main subject of his conversation with his Argentine counterpart, Pablo Quirno, and denied discussing with him Uruguay's interest in acquiring British ships

Uruguay's Foreign Minister Mario Lubetkin argued that the Falklands dispute has changed in nature with oil exploration: one thing, he said, is “the invaded island” and “the fight against colonialism”, and another is “when a lot of money is taken from there”. His remarks come as Yamandú Orsi's government considers buying two patrol vessels from the Royal Navy, a deal that has already prompted a resolution from twenty deputies of Argentine President Javier Milei's party.

“When the process of oil prospecting by the United Kingdom began in the islands, the whole logic of the Malvinas issue changed,” he said on Wednesday on Canal 10's Arriba Gente programme, referring to the economic use of a territory he described as “taken colonially”. “That means that behind it comes military articulation, because you will try to defend those funds,” he said, calling for a move to “another phase” that includes reflection by the political system. He also said Argentina “is defending its rights and its heritage”.

The minister said this was the main subject of his conversation with his Argentine counterpart, Pablo Quirno, and denied discussing with him Uruguay's interest in acquiring British ships.

The United Kingdom has offered Uruguay three first-generation River-class offshore patrol vessels — HMS Tyne, HMS Mersey and HMS Severn — of which the defence ministry hopes to acquire up to two. A navy mission visited the Mersey in London in May, and a transfer could take place in 2028, when the Royal Navy retires them. No final decision has been taken. The search follows the cancellation in October 2025 of a contract with Spanish shipyard Cardama for two patrol vessels, which the government rescinded after finding “strong indications” of fraud.

The Uruguayan navy has raised technical objections, including the lack of a helicopter hangar. Opposition senator Javier García, a former defence minister, called the deal “more political than technical” and warned of the signal it would send to Buenos Aires in the current context.

In Argentina, deputy Damián Arabia and 19 other La Libertad Avanza lawmakers filed a draft resolution expressing “bewilderment and concern” over the possible purchase. “Our fraternal ties and Uruguay's historic, supportive and generous backing for the Malvinas Cause warrant avoiding this acquisition,” he wrote. The resolution is non-binding and the Argentine government has not lodged an official protest.

The remarks come amid an escalation. On Monday Argentina announced arbitration against the United Kingdom over the Sea Lion oil project; British Overseas Territories Minister Uma Kumaran replied on Wednesday that such conduct “raises questions” about Argentina's reliability as a partner. The United Kingdom maintains that the activity is governed by the archipelago's legislation in accordance with international law. In the 2013 referendum, on a 92% turnout, 99.8% of voters chose to retain the status of a British overseas territory.

World.title: The Spectator likens Milei's Falklands push to Galtieri's
World.content:
The Spectator likens Milei's Falklands push to Galtieri's

30th Wednesday, September 2026 - 23:01 UTC Full article

An opinion column published on Wednesday in the British weekly The Spectator likens Argentine President Javier Milei's campaign over the Falklands to that of dictator Leopoldo Galtieri in 1982, with the difference, its author argues, that the current government is using legal rather than military means. The piece, by law professor Andrew Tettenborn, is an argument of opinion rather than a report of new facts.

The columnist calls “lawfare” — the use of legal instruments for political ends — the arbitration Argentina announced on Monday over the Sea Lion oil project. He argues that the real aim is to reopen the sovereignty question, that Milei sees the United Kingdom as weak and divided, and that he is seeking a distraction from domestic difficulties. These are the author's assessments; he also directs personal characterisations at British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and at Milei himself.

The legal core of the column is its most concrete part: the author argues that Argentina's claim is in substance a territorial sovereignty dispute and that the international law of the sea tribunal has made clear it does not see that as its role. In previous cases, tribunals constituted under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea have declined to rule on sovereignty disputes, as in the 2015 arbitration between Mauritius and the United Kingdom over the Chagos Islands. The procedure Buenos Aires has announced is an Annex VII arbitration; from the Hamburg-based International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea, Argentina would only seek provisional measures while the arbitral tribunal is constituted.

The column contains inaccuracies. It places the environmental lawsuit against the project in Buenos Aires and suggests it was filed with Milei's tacit approval; it was filed on September 1, before the presidential address that launched the campaign, by the Falklands War Veterans Centre of La Plata and an association of environmental lawyers before the federal court in Río Grande, Tierra del Fuego. Nor is it confirmed that the criminal complaints cover Rockhopper executives, as the text states.

Tettenborn advises the British government to reject the claim and “hold our nerve”, and argues that international courts have lost impartiality. The British statement issued the same Wednesday, however, expressly invokes the Law of the Sea Convention as the legal framework for oil activity in the archipelago.

Argentina argues that unilateral exploitation contravenes UN General Assembly resolutions 2065 and 31/49 and that the residents' wishes do not settle the dispute. In the 2013 referendum, on a 92% turnout, 99.8% of voters chose to retain the status of a British overseas territory.

World.title: Mexico’s fastest-growing states aren’t the ones having the most children
World.content:
The 2025 Intercensal Survey by the National Institute of Statistics and Geography (INEGI) has revealed a paradox in Mexico’s new demographic map: The states that have seen the greatest population growth are not those with the highest fertility rates.

Mexico reached a population of 130.9 million in 2025 – the country’s highest population in history. However, the population grew at an average annual rate of just 0.7%, its slowest pace in recent decades, with growth concentrated in states in the north and southeast of the country.

Which states lead population growth?

According to INEGI, Baja California Sur led in population growth with an average annual rate of 3.4%, followed by Quintana Roo at 2.2%. Querétaro recorded 1.7%, while Nuevo León and Coahuila grew by 1.5% annually.

Population growth in Quintana Roo is a result of its population dynamics: For years, the state has recorded growth linked to an influx of people from other states and the expansion of its urban and tourist areas, among other factors.

The same pattern is observed in Baja California Sur. Meanwhile Baja California, Querétaro and Nuevo León are attracting new residents thanks to urbanization, employment and internal migration.

In contrast, Guerrero and Veracruz lost population, shrinking by -0.6% and -0.3%, respectively.

Which states have the highest and lowest fertility rate?

The states topping the growth rankings are not the same ones showing the highest fertility rates. The Intercensal Survey revealed that Chiapas had the highest fertility rate at 1.8 children per woman, followed by Guerrero (1.6) and Durango (1.5).

The contrast is particularly striking in Baja California Sur and Quintana Roo. Despite ranking at the top for population growth between 2020 and 2025, their fertility rates were among the lowest in the country — 1.2 and 1.1 children per woman, respectively.

Mexico City has the second largest population of any entity or state, despite having the lowest fertility rate (0.8). According to the survey, its population stands at 9.1 million, just behind México state, which with 17.5 million inhabitants is the most populous state in the country.

With reports from Uno TV

World.title: Mexico’s City’s chinampa restoration project Arca Tierra wins 2026 Champions of Change Award
World.content:
Arca Tierra, a Mexican sustainable agriculture initiative founded by brothers Lucio and Pablo Usobiaga, has won the Champions of Change Award 2026 by The World’s 50 Best Restaurants in Latin America.

The award honors their work to restore the chinampas of Xochimilco — an agricultural system set on man-made islands, used by the Mexica people in pre-Hispanic times. They are raised plots anchored to the lakebed, created from mud, organic matter, and vegetation.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by The 50 Best Restaurants (@theworlds50best)

Today they are known as a Mexico City tourist attraction due to the boat rides aboard traditional trajineras. But the Xochimilco chinampas remain part of the capital’s productive and cultural landscape

They face, however, challenges, such as environmental degradation, urban expansion, and declining profitability for those who work the land.

Arca Tierra seeks to improve their condition to create a food supply chain that is fairer, local and regenerative. Their project seeks to produce high-quality food with a lower environmental impact, preserve traditional farming knowledge, and expand access to local products for restaurants, consumers, and communities in Mexico City.

“This recognition confirms that we are on the right track and inspires us to continue working hard with the farmers and producers that collaborate with us,” Lucio said in a statement.

In the capital, Arca Tierra produces around five tonnes of food per hectare per month. Its harvests supply 47 restaurants in Mexico City and reach more than 300 families through weekly baskets.

The initiative has also developed culinary and rural tourism offerings designed to connect chefs, diners, and visitors with the origins of their food. Its projects include Baldío—a Mexico City restaurant created in collaboration with British chef Douglas McMaster—which focuses on comprehensive use of ingredients and on waste reduction. For example, vegetable peels are fermented to make a traditional beverage called tepache, or repurposed into a syrup that is then diluted and fermented before being incorporated into other dishes.

Ultimately, Arca Tierra seeks to turn the spotlight to a process often overlooked by diners — the production and sourcing of local ingredients.

“In the value chain, the person who produces the food earns the least money — it’s a total contradiction because they’re the most important of all,” Pablo said.

With the mission to bring quality produce to more people, Arca Tierra has expanded its vision beyond Xochimilco and it now operates in Huasca de Ocampo, Hidalgo, and Amanalco de Becerra and Polvillos, in México state.

With reports from El Estímulo and Cool Hunter Mx

World.title: Ebrard, in Milwaukee, strikes optimistic note on USMCA talks —’closer every day’
World.content:
Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard remains bullish about ongoing Mexico-U.S. trade talks, saying on Thursday that he is optimistic that new agreements are in the offing.

“We are getting closer on many issues, resolving problems, and we are making progress,” he said. “Every day we are closer to reaching new agreements.”

Ebrard spoke to reporters on the sidelines of the G-20 meeting in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, after a one-hour meeting with his U.S. counterpart Jamieson Greer.

Despite U.S. President Donald Trump’s protectionist policies, his tariffs and his lukewarm attitude toward the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA), Mexican exports to the U.S. continue to grow at a double-digit rate and bilateral trade is approaching US $900 billion annually.

Ebrard said his main priorities are negotiating the reduction of Section 232 tariffs, which affect Mexican exports of automobiles and other materials such as steel, aluminum and copper, and maintaining the preferential tariff treatment currently enjoyed by Mexican shipments that meet the requirements of the USMCA.

Even with the changes Washington is pushing for in its trade policy, Ebrard insists Mexico will maintain an advantageous position.

Comparing Mexico’s situation with representatives from Turkey, Saudi Arabia and other nations present at the G-20, Ebrard said “I was able to confirm that we are in a more favorable situation than they are.”

Ebrard attributed Mexico’s preferential status to President Claudia Sheinbaum’s handling of relations with Trump and to the close economic integration on both sides of their shared border.

An unnamed Mexican official cited by France 24 television network supported Ebrard’s optimism regarding the tariff talks.

“We expect to have reductions in steel and cars and aluminum,” the official said, speaking on condition of anonymity.

When asked if a deal would be struck before critical midterm elections in the U.S. next month, the official said Mexico is content to be patient.

In addition to meeting with Greer, Ebrard took advantage of the G-20 summit to strengthen ties with the European Union, Canada, India, Japan and Argentina.

“Our primary objective here at the summit has been to … protect jobs, our companies and our interests,” he said.

He is now planning trade missions to the EU and Canada next year, while confirming that Mexico and India are poised to begin a “new stage” in their economic relationship, with discussions ranging from tequila, which is subject to a 150% tariff, to vehicles and auto parts.

With reports from El País, EFE, France 24, LatinUS and El Economista

World.title: Former Navy officer ‘Capitán Sol’ arrested in Jalisco for fuel smuggling
World.content:
Miguel Ángel Solano Ruiz, a key participant in the fuel-smuggling scheme that has tarnished the Navy, was arrested in Zapopan, Jalisco, on Thursday night.

Solano Ruiz, aka “Capitán Sol,” is a retired Marine captain and purportedly one of the main operators of the fuel smuggling network allegedly orchestrated by the Farías Laguna brothers, both of whom were high-ranking Navy officers.

El traslado de Miguel Ángel Solano Ruiz, “El Capitán Sol” o “Mike”, señalado como uno de los principales operadores de la red de huachicol fiscal que involucró a mandos de la Marina y funcionarios de aduanas, quien fue detenido en Zapopan, Jalisco. pic.twitter.com/r6nLMvLVBo — REFORMA (@Reforma) October 2, 2026

According to witness testimony, Solano recruited active-duty and retired naval personnel to participate in the network that smuggled hydrocarbons through customs without paying the corresponding taxes, a crime known in Mexico as huachicol fiscal.

He allegedly used his influence within the Navy to place these men in key positions at maritime customs offices in ports such as Tampico, Altamira, Ensenada and Guaymas, while also corrupting public officials through bribes.

The Federal Attorney General’s Office (FGR) says Solano, 48, is the last remaining key player of the Farías Laguna criminal organization and will face organized crime and tax evasion charges.

The corruption scheme was uncovered when authorities seized a vessel carrying 10 million liters of diesel smuggled from Texas off the coast of Tamaulipas in March 2024.

Vice Admiral Manuel Roberto Farías Laguna was arrested on Sept. 2, 2025, while his brother Fernando, a rear admiral, remained a fugitive until he was captured in Argentina in April and deported to Mexico on Aug. 21 this year.

While serving in the Navy, Solano held several positions related to intelligence at Central Command and retired in 2018 with a pension of 18,000 pesos per month.

However, investigators found that his lifestyle greatly exceeded that pension: He lost more than 52 million pesos (US $2.5 million) on gambling, while casinos and racetracks had issued 400 warnings about him to the authorities. He also owned eight properties in Veracruz and Mexico City valued at over 13 million pesos (US $714,000).

Investigations over the course of the past year led authorities to addresses in France, Greece, Monaco and Spain, before the net closed around the suspect in Jalisco.

Authorities said that following more than 300 days in pursuit of Solano, a search warrant was issued on Thursday for a property located in the Villa Verona subdivision of Zapopan, a suburb of Guadalajara.

During the search, an arrest warrant was issued and Solano was apprehended. He was transferred to the Altiplano maximum-security prison in México state on Friday.

With reports from El Economista, El País, El Financiero and Proceso

World.title: After its September nosedive, is the super peso gone for good?
World.content:
The peso weakened 6.32% in September, its largest monthly depreciation since June 2024, pressured by monetary tightening and the less attractive interest rate differential with the United States.

Last month’s poor performance has prompted the question of whether the phenomenon known as the “super peso” has run its course or is merely suffering a setback.

Mexico’s currency had demonstrated unexpected strength in recent months, but the US dollar strengthened after the U.S. Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate to 4% on Sept. 16.

The dollar recovery extended pressure on the peso, which was already suffering from fluctuating oil prices and risks of a broader war in the Middle East, adding an inflationary component and complicating the monetary policy outlook while increasing market volatility.

When Mexico’s central bank kept its rate steady at 6.50% on Sept. 24 — reducing the spread between the two countries to just 250 basis points — the peso’s decline intensified as long-term U.S. bond yields climbed to multi-year highs.

The smaller spread weakened one of the supports of the “super peso,” reducing the appeal of “carry trade” operations, which for much of 2025 and the first half of this year generated demand for pesos.

Janeth Quiroz, a Grupo Financiero Monex analyst, warned that the carry-trade mechanism can now work in the opposite direction, telling El Economista that as the additional return decreases, the incentive to hold positions in pesos falls.

But although a stronger dollar and high yields on U.S. Treasury bonds add exchange rate pressure, Quiroz insisted it might be more accurate to speak of a loss of strength of the super peso rather than of its “definitive end.”

BBVA Mexico chief economist Carlos Serrano attributed the depreciation to external factors, pointing to the uncertainty surrounding the USMCA free trade deal.

He identified fiscal discipline and greater depth of the domestic financial market as supporting factors, suggesting the peso is still relatively strong and perhaps even overvalued.

For Mexican households, the depreciation cuts both ways. Families receiving dollar remittances gain purchasing power, while imported goods and fuel can become more expensive if the weaker peso lasts.

As October started, the peso closed at 18.30 per US dollar on Thursday, slipping 1.29%, but was up 0.67% at 1:30 p.m. Friday, trading at 18.1808.

And despite the recent jump above 18 pesos, the latest consensus from the central bank and Citi Mexico anticipates an appreciation to 17.50 pesos per US dollar by the end of 2026.

With reports from El Economista, EFE, El Financiero and Expansión

World.title: El Jalapeño: Mexico blasts France for delay in returning a book it borrowed 166 years ago
World.content:
All stories in El Jalapeño are satire and not real news. Check out the original article here.

A cross-Atlantic rift is developing as Mexican cultural officials have accused counterparts in France of borrowing a book and not returning it for 166 years.

In a harshly worded statement, Emiliano Muñoz of Mexico’s National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH) has accused the National Library of France of perfectly personifying Charles Lamb’s description of book borrowers as “mutilators of collections and spoilers of the symmetry of shelves.”

Muñoz confirmed that repeated pleas by INAH for the National Library of France to return the Azcatitlan Codex — a priceless Mexica codex which it has possessed since the late 19th century — were always met with assurances that it intended to. But “something always came up.”

“That excuse is good for 70, maybe 80 years,” Muñoz said. “But once you hit 16 decades, it suggests bad faith.”

He also addressed France’s earlier assertion that it assumed the book was a gift. “Come on!” said an exasperated Muñoz. “You take a book from a friend’s house, you bring it back. That’s how it works. The fact that nobody ever does is no excuse.”

Reached for comment via WhatsApp, Jean-Luc Pierre-François de la Tour-du-Pin Baguette-Chauchard, director of the National Library of France, posted an eye-rolling emoji before countering the assertion: “It’s not like Mexico is a spotless borrower,” he said. “We sent them an emperor who wasn’t even ours to lend. And did they return him? No! They shot him.”

“Besides,” added Tour-du-Pin Baguette-Chauchard. “I never read the book. You know why? There were no words in it. It was a picture book. Sacré bleu!”

With no détente in sight, Muñoz said INAH will seek a new book-exchange partner who won’t spoil the symmetry of its shelves. “The National Library of France is lucky we’re not holding them to their own regulations,” Muñoz pointed out. “Or they would owe us €68 million in late fees.”
