World.title: Russia ‘tearing Kyiv apart’, mayor says, as strikes paralyse traffic
World.content:
Kyiv – Russian attacks on key infrastructure were “tearing Kyiv apart”, the city’s mayor said Friday, as strikes on a bridge linking the capital’s east and west brought traffic to a standstill.

President Volodymyr Zelensky accused his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, of ripping up the rulebook of armed conflict by sanctioning massive attacks on civilian areas, an accusation the Kremlin has rejected.

The grinding conflict, which began with Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, has largely focused on ground fighting in the east, with Kyiv largely spared from the devastation wrought near the frontline.

But Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said the city should now be on a war footing.

“The capital is in a very dramatic situation,” he posted on Telegram. “It’s no longer possible to pretend that we can live now as we lived in peacetime.

“The enemy is tearing Kyiv apart.”

His message came as the authorities shut one of Kyiv’s main bridges and restricted movement on a second after another wave of deadly strikes by fast-moving, jet-powered drones.

Long lines of stationary cars and buses were gridlocked on main roads as commuters sought alternative routes — or even made their way on foot.

“I’ve been travelling for three hours… to get to work,” said Tetiana Osypenko, a 49-year-old seamstress whose bus was stuck in a traffic jam.

“There’s just no way to get there. Nothing. It’s impossible to cross the bridges today,” she told AFP.

Traffic built up due to the complete closure to all vehicles going in both directions on the Southern Bridge, one of eight bridges connecting the east and west of Kyiv over the Dnipro river.

It was hit several times on Thursday and Friday morning.

The Paton Bridge, further north, was open in one direction only, though there were no reports that it had been struck.

In a post on X, Zelensky accused Putin of last month declaring there were “no rules now”, citing unnamed intelligence and people around Putin.

“The Russians couldn’t occupy us. So now they are doing massive attacks and massive killings,” Zelensky said.

The Kremlin made no immediate public response to the claim, which Zelensky first made in an interview with the Financial Times.

– Daily disruption –

Kyiv has been increasingly under aerial bombardment in recent months, putting the city on near-constant alert and disrupting daily life.

Air raid sirens warning of approaching threats in the skies sound almost round the clock, urging the city’s estimated three million people to seek shelter.

Repeated strikes on trains and petrol stations have already hit the rail and road networks while attacks on energy facilities threaten power and heating as winter approaches.

Osypenko, the seamstress, said she would not get home because of the traffic jams. Previous disruption to subway services during air raids forced her to spend the night in a metro station near the Southern Bridge.

Not being able to work costs her money, compounding the financial pressures caused by the war, she added. “You just spend the whole day feeling completely beaten down.”

The latest Russian attacks killed one person and wounded at least two other people when a 25-storey residential building was hit in southeast Kyiv.

– ‘Political will’ –

Zelensky urged tougher sanctions to prevent Russia from manufacturing its new jet-powered drones, which are faster and harder to intercept.

Russia’s production of the weapons was “critically dependent” on foreign components, he wrote on social media on Friday.

“Every Russian drone can actually be stopped right at the production line. What is needed is the political will of these countries,” he added.

Zelensky has repeatedly called on Ukraine’s Western allies for more military support, particularly for US-made Patriot missile interceptors.

On Thursday, he said Ukraine had used its FP-7 tactical ballistic missile in combat for the first time, without disclosing where or what it had been used against.

He also said Ukraine was testing five of its own interceptors against drones.

Ukraine’s military on Friday said it struck an oil refinery in Volgograd and another facility in Samara, both in southwest Russia, for allegedly supplying fuel to Russian forces.

Kyiv also dismissed reports that its F-16 fighter jets — another key tool used against jet-powered drones — could be grounded due to delays in maintenance inspection and the supply of parts.

But Zelensky told the Financial Times that around half of Ukraine’s fleet was spending lengthy maintenance periods in Europe.

World.title: Man City verdict a ‘big topic’ for England players, says Tuchel
World.content:
London – Thomas Tuchel said that Manchester City were the talk of the England camp after the club were found guilty of multiple breaches of Premier League financial rules, but insisted that the case would not affect his selection for Saturday’s match in Croatia.

The findings by an independent commission, announced earlier this week, have sent shockwaves through English football.

City, the dominant Premier League force over the past 15 years, face severe sanctions, which could include expulsion from the top division.

Marc Guehi and Elliott Anderson are the only two City players remaining in Tuchel’s squad for the Nations League match in Rijeka after Nico O’Reilly was forced to withdraw due to injury.

“We had some time off and some time between the matches, and it’s a big subject,” Tuchel told his pre-match press conference on Friday.

“Of course the players talk about it, and City players talk about it, and we talk to them, but only briefly.

“They’re ready to go for tomorrow, that’s what they show on the pitch and that’s what they show in camp, but of course it’s a big topic.”

City deny wrongdoing and on Friday lodged an appeal against the ruling.

But unless they can overturn the decision of the commission, they are likely to face at least a points deduction, which would threaten their place in the Premier League.

Tuchel was asked if the club’s players would still be in his mind for selection should they be playing regularly in the lower divisions.

“There’s always a possibility,” he said. “I think I would always try to pick the best team for the camp, for the occasion, for the tournament, and I will never rule out that they don’t play in the top flight in their country.

“So we need to look at this from case by case.”

England’s clash with Croatia, which will take place behind closed doors, is their third of four Nations League games in the current international window.

The Three Lions were beaten 3-2 by world champions Spain on home soil last weekend, but bounced back to beat the Czech Republic 2-0 on Tuesday.

World.title: US posts weak job growth data in September
World.content:
Washington – Employment in the United States grew by 29,000 jobs in September, missing analysts’ expectations significantly, with the unemployment rate rising slightly to 4.2 percent, government data showed on Friday.

Adding to the weak data, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) also revised down job figures for July and August by a combined 60,000 jobs, the department said in a statement.

The revision to July’s data showed that the world’s largest economy lost jobs that month, as opposed to posting a gain of 21,000 as previously reported.

The data comes ahead of key midterm elections in November where President Donald Trump’s Republican Party is facing a stern test over his handling of the economy.

Analysts polled by Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal had expected the US economy to add 84,000 jobs in September.

– Health care leads –

Employment in most major sectors was largely unchanged, the BLS reported, with health care posting notable gains of 17,000.

The sector has propped up the labor market in the United States in the last year, as an aging population requires more care both in hospitals and at home.

Still, September’s gains in the sector were slower than its average monthly gain of 33,000 over the last year.

The financial sector continued its downward slide, losing 7,000 jobs in September and bringing its overall slump from a recent peak in May 2025 to 129,000.

Most of the losses in that sector have been among insurance companies.

– Fed implications –

Average hourly earnings for all employees were up 3.0 percent, the BLS said, with wages continuing to lag behind stubbornly high inflation — meaning most workers are seeing real wage losses.

Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren seized on the data to criticize Trump’s performance since taking office last year.

“Paychecks are growing at their slowest rate in nearly seven years, outside of the Covid-19 pandemic,” she said in a statement.

“Since the start of Trump’s war, real wages have fallen 0.7 percent as his failed agenda keeps pushing prices up,” she said, referring to the US war against Iran launched in late February.

The conflict has plunged the Middle East into violence and sent global energy prices skyrocketing, as Tehran’s retaliatory action has targeted Washington’s regional allies and choked a key trading route.

The data comes after the US Federal Reserve — which has a dual mandate to maintain inflation at a long-term two-percent target while ensuring maximum employment — raised interest rates last month to address high prices.

The US labor market has been largely in balance this year, with modest job gains and a relatively steady unemployment rate.

That steadiness has allowed the Fed to focus on the inflation side of its mandate, but any weakness in the labor market may give policy makers pause.

Raising interest rates tends to cool inflation but can also limit economic activity, which can affect the job market.

This week, two key Fed policymakers indicated that the central bank may not raise rates again at its October meeting, although markets continue to expect a further hike before the end of the year.

Friday’s jobs data “lends support to the less hawkish Fed officials that indicate no need to rush and deliver the next rate hike at the end of this month,” said Kathy Bostjancic, chief economist at Nationwide, in a note.

She added that this could release some pressure on bond yields — which have been spiralling in part due to expectations of interest rate hikes.

Nancy Vanden Houten at Oxford Economics, however, disagreed, expecting upside risks to inflation to continue to dominate Fed policymakers’ thinking.

“We think the upside risks to inflation are still a bigger concern for the Federal Reserve and expect they will raise rates at the end of the month,” she said.

World.title: Ethiopia’s conflict: the regional dimension
World.content:
Addis Ababa – Renewed fighting between the Ethiopian government and Tigrayan rebels has worsened regional tensions, with Ethiopia and Eritrea breaking diplomatic ties on Thursday.

Heavy fighting resumed between federal forces and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) last week, and fighting has been ongoing across several fronts in northern Ethiopia.

The geopolitics of the Horn of Africa are fiendishly complex, with shifting alliances and the involvement of many outside actors with conflicting interests.

Here is what is at stake for the countries concerned:

– Eritrea –

Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing the TPLF, including with troops, which it has denied.

On Thursday, they expelled each other’s diplomats and shut down their respective embassies.

Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993, and the two sides fought a brutal border war between 1998 and 2000.

Relations improved markedly with the rise of Ethiopia’s Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed in 2018, and Eritrea even fought alongside Ethiopia during the last civil war against the TPLF in 2020-2022.

But relations have since cratered, with Eritrea fearing landlocked Ethiopia plans to invade and seize access to the Red Sea.

“The TPLF is silently allied with its former foe, Eritrea, with supply lines chiefly secured through Tigray’s northern border,” the Chatham House think tank said in a report.

Eritrea’s “priority is to keep war away from its own territory”, it added, before cautioning the country’s actions increase the risk of regional escalation.

– Sudan –

The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have close ties with the TPLF and Eritrea. Tigrayan fighters have reportedly fought with the SAF in Sudan’s civil war.

Ethiopia is accused of assisting the United Arab Emirates in supplying the SAF’s opponent, the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which it has denied.

Sudan was accused of funnelling weapons and supplies to the TPLF during the last war. There were clashes along the shared border in August, suggesting it remains an active concern for the Ethiopian government.

– Egypt –

Egypt is strongly opposed to Ethiopia’s new Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, which it says will affect downstream Nile waters. It has forged closer ties with Eritrea and Somalia in an apparent anti-Ethiopia front.

Ethiopia expelled an Egyptian diplomat on Thursday, without giving a reason. Cairo responded by expelling an Ethiopian diplomat.

– United Arab Emirates –

The UAE has invested deeply across east Africa as it seeks security partnerships to counter rivals and control the Red Sea, as well as agricultural land, and investments.

It has been one of Abiy’s principal backers, giving him a $3 billion loan and investment package when he came to power in 2018, and building his giant new palace in Addis Ababa, as well as providing military drones and logistical support during the last civil war.

In return, it is alleged that Ethiopia has helped funnel arms to the UAE’s allies in Sudan, though that is denied by both countries.

– United States –

Washington was closely involved in the peace deal that ended the last civil war in 2022.

Its focus has lately been on the Red Sea — and its efforts to contain Iran and its proxies. As a result, it allowed sanctions on Ethiopia and Eritrea to end, with the ill-timed claim that the “national emergency… has expired”.

– Somalia –

Ethiopia’s relations with Somalia were ruptured in January 2024 when Addis Ababa signed a sea-access deal with the breakaway region of Somaliland.

Relations were ultimately restored with Turkish mediation and the deal with Somaliland seemingly put on the back burner.

World.title: Swiss president to quit government
World.content:
Geneva – Swiss President Guy Parmelin announced Friday that he will quit the government at the end of the year, in a sudden move after more than a decade of ministerial service.

Switzerland’s presidency rotates annually among the seven members of the government, called the Federal Council, of which Parmelin, 66, was the longest-serving minister.

Parmelin told a press conference in Bern that he had informed ministerial colleagues of his decision to step down on December 31.

“By then, it will have been 11 years since I was elected to this role, and the time has come for me to make way for new energy in these times of great uncertainty,” he said, admitting to feeling “a certain weariness”, while insisting he was not stepping down for medical reasons.

– Tariff tussle with Trump –

A pragmatist, Parmelin seemed to make more headway with US President Donald Trump than his predecessor Karin Keller-Sutter.

Trump shocked Switzerland in August 2025 when he announced 39-percent duties on imports of Swiss goods, among the highest in his global tariff blitz.

Parmelin, the economy minister, went to Washington three times in a bid to reduce the rate.

Eventually, Switzerland and the United States announced a declaration of intent to cut tariffs to 15 percent, with the Swiss vowing to invest $200 billion in the United States.

A winegrower by trade, Parmelin is from the French-speaking western canton of Vaud. He is from the hard-right Swiss People’s Party (SVP), which is the biggest in the country,

Parmelin was previously president in 2021 and took centre-stage as Switzerland hosted a summit in Geneva between Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Joe Biden.

The president of the Swiss Confederation is first among equals on the Federal Council, chairs its meetings and typically represents the country in major domestic and international matters.

The position goes to whoever has had the longest run on the council without being president.

Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis will become president in 2027.

Parmelin joined the Federal Council in 2016 as defence minister and has held the economy brief since 2019.

The Federal Council seven seats are shared 2-2-2-1 among the four main political parties under a decades-old tacit agreement known as “the magic formula”.

Parmelin’s successor will come from the SVP. Candidates have until October 23 to come forward, and parliament will choose on December 9.

Parmelin will visit India for a three-day state visit from Monday.

World.title: Pilot in flydubai attack says could not let ‘all those people die’
World.content:
Dubai – An Indian pilot attacked by his co-pilot aboard a flight from the UAE to Israel said Friday that he “could not let all those people die”, in his first public remarks after he helped stop the plane from crashing.

His actions on Wednesday helped avert disaster when he managed to open the cockpit door despite suffering injuries, allowing passengers and crew to take control of the plane and make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

The co-pilot has been returned to the United Arab Emirates, where the incident is under investigation to determine any “terrorist activity or intent”.

The mostly Israeli passengers on the flight have been flown back to Israel on a replacement plane.

Flydubai captain Smit Machchhar told Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a call from his hospital bed that he knew he had to act quickly, saying his opening the cockpit door was a “last push” to get help.

“I had suffered so many injuries that I had collapsed. At that time, I could feel that the aircraft was going down. I knew this was the last push, that the door was right there,” he said.

“I was being hit even then, but I just opened the door and everyone came in.”

Machchhar, who has 17 years of aviation experience — 11 as a captain — described the moment he realised the plane was going down while he was lying injured.

He told Modi that during the ordeal, he had recited a Hindu devotional prayer dedicated to the deity Hanuman.

“I know God himself saved me,” he said.

He said years of aviation experience allowed him to understand what was happening even while he was wounded.

– ‘Kill me, kill me’ –

The circumstances of the confrontation are under investigation, but the co-pilot allegedly attacked Machchhar, leaving him wounded and triggering a struggle for control of the aircraft.

Passengers described rushing the cockpit and a fight for control after the plane suddenly plummeted — losing around 17,000 feet of altitude in the span of a minute, according to the Flightradar24 website.

Modi said Machchhar’s actions helped save many lives and avert “a great tragedy”.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu earlier also credited Machchhar, as well as the flight’s passengers, with averting catastrophe.

US President Donald Trump warned on Thursday that if Iran was found to be linked to the attack the country would be “hit very hard”.

Netanyahu has said the suspect had undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination”.

“The attacker, he calls out to the aircrew, ‘Kill me, kill me’,” Netanyahu told US media, adding it was “clear he was suicidal”.

The Israeli leader identified the co-pilot as an Omani national and said Israel would check how he had been cleared to work on flights to the country.

“We have constraints that say that you can’t have pilots from countries that don’t have diplomatic relations with Israel. Obviously he was able to go through that,” Netanyahu told Fox News.

Flydubai has suspended flights to and from Israel since the attack, leaving some Israelis stranded in the UAE.

Israel’s flag carrier El Al is planning replacement flights to bring them home but was forced to cancel them Friday, saying Emirati authorities had not given landing permission.

“As soon as approval is received from the authorities, we are prepared to carry out the special flights to Dubai and return the Israelis home as soon as possible,” El Al said in an online notice.

World.title: Disney president says layoffs ‘extremely painful’ but necessary
World.content:
Los Angeles – The Walt Disney Company’s President Dana Walden said on Thursday that the company’s layoffs were “extremely painful” but necessary for its survival.

Disney has carried out several rounds of cost cutting measures in recent years to combat intense competition in streaming, while advances in AI tools have also become a cheaper production alternative for the billion-dollar company.

“We’ve exited colleagues who I’ve worked with for most of my career… It is in many ways a harsh reality,” Walden said during the Bloomberg Screentime conference in Los Angeles.

“It is extremely painful,” she added.

More than 300 people were laid off from Disney on Tuesday, most of whom work in human resources and information technology, according to US media reports.

It comes after Disney eliminated around 1,000 positions in April, primarily across the company’s marketing group, following the arrival of new chief executive Josh D’Amaro, trade media reported.

Walden said the company had also offered a group of executives “the opportunity to make their own decision around whether the timing was right to leave or to stay” as part of a voluntary retirement plan. It remains unclear if the latest wave of layoffs made use of the initiative.

“There is a need to constantly evaluate how you’re structured,” Walden said about Disney and its competitors in the technology industry.

“Technology set their sights on our business, and we must survive and thrive and grow. And that’s what we’re going to do,” she said.

The Walt Disney company did not immediately reply to a request for comment.

World.title: Indian flydubai pilot opened cockpit door to save passengers
World.content:
New Delhi – Indian flydubai captain Smit Machchhar knew he had to act quickly after an alleged in-flight attack by his co-pilot, opening the cockpit door in a “last push” to get help and avert disaster, he said Friday.

“I was trying to save my own life, but I knew I could not let all those people die,” Machchhar said during a call from his hospital bed to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, according to a video posted by the leader on social media.

The Boeing 737 flight to Tel Aviv, operated by Dubai-based flydubai, was carrying 174 passengers when the altercation took place on Wednesday.

Machchhar, who has 17 years of aviation experience — 11 as a captain — described the moment he realised the plane was going down while he was lying injured.

“I had suffered so many injuries that I had collapsed. At that time, I could feel that the aircraft was going down. I knew this was the last push, that the door was right there,” he said.

“I was being hit even then, but I just opened the door and everyone came in.”

Machchhar told Modi that during the ordeal, he had recited a Hindu devotional prayer dedicated to the deity Hanuman.

“I know God himself saved me,” he said.

Machchhar said years of aviation experience allowed him to understand what was happening even while he was injured.

The circumstances of the confrontation are under investigation.

– ‘Very proud’ –

The co-pilot allegedly attacked Machchhar, leaving him wounded and triggering a struggle for control of the aircraft.

Passengers described rushing the cockpit and a fight for control after the plane suddenly plummeted — losing around 17,000 feet of altitude in the span of a minute, according to the Flightradar24 website — before eventually making an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

Modi said Machchhar’s actions helped save many lives and avert “a great tragedy”.

“You have done such a great thing that people across the country and around the world are eager to see you and speak to you,” Modi told him.

“You have truly made the whole country proud.”

Machchhar became emotional during the conversation, telling Modi that he felt proud of himself for the first time since the incident.

“I am feeling very proud right now. I had not felt proud of myself until now,” he said.

The pilot, his head wrapped in bandages, and with a breathing tube in his nose, said the path to recovery was long.

“I am not thinking of it as a wound, I am thinking of it as a journey,” he said.

“And it will take time, but I am very, very confident that I will recover.”

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu earlier credited Machchhar, as well as the flight’s passengers, with averting catastrophe.

World.title: 5 Indian seafarers safely rescued after Kuwait-flagged tanker struck by projectile in Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Five Indian nationals aboard a Kuwait-flagged crude oil tanker were safely rescued after the vessel was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, the Indian embassy in Oman said on Friday.

The Indian nationals were aboard MT Kazimah III, which was hit while sailing through the strategic waterway. The embassy coordinated their rescue and said all five had been safely shifted ashore.

âEarlier today, the Mission coordinated rescue of five Indian nationals on board the Kuwait-flagged tanker MT Kazimah III, struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz. All 5 Indian nationals have been shifted ashore safely.

We thank the Omani authorities for their continued support and assistance,â the embassy said in a post on X.

The embassy thanked Omani authorities for their support during the rescue operation.

MT Kazimah III is a crude oil tanker sailing under the Kuwaiti flag and was en route to the port of LomÃ© in Togo when it was struck.

The incident comes as India steps up efforts to monitor the safety of its seafarers amid heightened security risks in the Persian Gulf and other major shipping routes.





Earlier on Tuesday, external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that more than 4,500 Indian seafarers were aboard commercial vessels operating in the region. Of these, 163 were on 12 active cargo ships, including six India-flagged vessels and six foreign-flagged vessels carrying cargo to India.

âAt this point, we have six India-flagged commercial vessels in the Persian Gulf. We also have six foreign-flagged vessels which are carrying cargo to India.

So 12 ships are there. On these ships, we have around 163 Indian seafarers who are on board,â Jaiswal said during a media briefing.

âApart from this, we also have over 4,500 Indian seafarers who are on board various commercial vessels which are operating in the area,â he added.

Jaiswal said the ministry of shipping was coordinating with Indian diplomatic missions and local stakeholders to track vessel movements and monitor the welfare of Indian seafarers.

âOur ministry of shipping continues to monitor the movement of these ships and is looking at the well-being of all these seafarers, and as and when required, through our embassies and other stakeholders, they do the needful for their well-being and welfare,â he stated.

âOn our side, we remain committed to the safety and well-being of our seafaring community abroad,â Jaiswal said.

The incident comes amid growing risks to commercial shipping across the Persian Gulf, Red Sea and Black Sea, where vessels have faced repeated attacks.

External affairs minister S Jaishankar had raised concerns over attacks on commercial vessels and seafarers during his address to the 81st United Nations general assembly last week.

âNew challenges in the maritime domain have added to longstanding ones on land. There have been attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers in the Gulf and from the Red Sea to the Black Sea. Indian seafarers have lost their lives, as have others from other nations.

This is completely unacceptable,â Jaishankar told the UN assembly.

Jaishankar said India had joined Liberia and 23 partner nations in an international coalition aimed at mobilising global public opinion and defending commercial shipping routes.

âWe must ensure that the safety and security of shipping and seafarers is never compromised. Scrupulously observing international law is an integral element of that endeavour,â Jaishankar urged.

He also called for immediate restraint and de-escalation in the Gulf to protect civilian crews and ensure the uninterrupted movement of energy supplies and global trade.

World.title: India reviews security SOPs, measures after flydubai event
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Indian security and intelligence establishment is on alert following the failed hijacking of a flydubai flight, undertaking a confidential evaluation of SOPs and security measures in place for the aviation sector, sources said.

In response to new hijacking threats, security authorities are reassessing both ground-level passenger screening, cockpit access vulnerabilities and in-flight countermeasures.

They aim to ascertain whether existing in-flight security measures like two-person cockpit presence mandates and physical barrier protocols require reinforcement.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

While Indian authorities are not directly involved in investigating the flydubai incident, intelligence agencies are closely monitoring developments after initial findings attributed the hijacking attempt to radicalisation.

In the aftermath of the attack - in which Captain Smit Machchhar thwarted an attempted mid-air sabotage by his co-pilot - the agencies are actively coordinating with counter-terrorism partners in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Israel, primarily focussing on intelligence-sharing.

The priority, sources said, was to obtain and analyse background, digital footprint and potential extremist affiliations of the suspect to ascertain whether the incident was an isolated act of radicalisation or part of a broader network targeting sensitive West Asian flight corridors.

World.title: From hospital bed, Captain Smit tells PM Modi: Couldn’t let others die
World.content:
Bleeding on the cockpit floor after being attacked by his co-pilot, Captain Smit Machchhar said his thoughts were fixed on saving all 174 passengers as the assailant frenetically tried to crash the aircraft.

Drawing strength from Hanuman Chalisa, he made a final push to open the cockpit door, allowing others to overpower the attacker and steer the plane to safety.

In his first publicly available account, Machchhar spoke from his Abu Dhabi hospital bed to PM Narendra Modi by video call Friday. âI was fighting for my life, but I was determined not to let others die. There was a moment when I was lying down, when I realised that the plane was going down,â he said.

Machchhar said he had told himself to get up and act. âI have been flying planes for 17 years, I have been a captain for the last 11 years, and I know what is happening in an aircraft even with my eyes closed... I was being attacked, but I made a last push and opened the door,â he said, praising those who rushed into the cockpit and seized the violent co-pilot.

Raw emotions took over him for a while as Machchhar spoke to Modi about those dramatic moments and called him his idol.





The PM responded that his courage had made Smit a global hero, with people worldwide offering prayers for his good health, and shown that Indians save lives rather than take them. âYou have boosted the prestige of 140 crore Indians,â Modi said, adding: âYou saved everyone. Youâve done a very great job.

â

Modi also thanked govts of Saudi Arabia and UAE for caring for Machchhar. Referring to social media reactions, he said people wondered what India and its pilots might have suffered without Machchharâs intervention.

Some online posts suggested that if the Omani co-pilot had succeeded, uncertainty over responsibility could have fuelled dark speculation and doubts about the Indian pilot.

âToday is Gandhi Jayanti. You have shown the world what the true meaning of âahimsaâ is,â Modi said. He later posted the call online with the message: âAn unforgettable conversation with Captain Smit, filled with pride and emotions.â

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Machchhar said the call lifted his morale: âReceiving a call from you makes me feel so proud.

Now I feel proud of myself too. I did not have this feeling so far. I am sorry I am crying in front of you.â

When Machchhar said he had never imagined speaking to Modi, the PM replied that his deed had made people worldwide eager to see and speak to him. Modi briefly spoke to him in Gujarati and said the country was eager to greet him after his recovery.

Machchhar said work may keep him outside India but not away from its culture. He performs puja each morning and recites Hanuman Chalisa with his two-yearold son on his lap. Modi praised his familyâs values and his parentsâ composure

World.title: UAE terms flydubai stabbing 'terrorist act', hails Indian pilot
World.content:
Captain Smit Machchharâs professionalism and moral sense in the darkest of circumstances make him a true hero, UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash said.

Grateful to Machchhar, a true hero of India: Israeli envoy

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Calling the flydubai incident a dangerous terrorist act, UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash lauded Indian co-pilot Smit Machchhar's critical role in preventing an air disaster by describing him as a true hero.The remarks suggest that the UAE is not going to downplay the attack, while also serving as the first official acknowledgement by the UAE government of the remarkable fightback by Machchhar against his Omani co-pilot under extreme pressure.Gargash's comments, which came in the middle of the probe to ascertain if the incident was indeed linked to terrorism, followed the announcement by Israeli ambassador to India Reuven Azar that Israel will suitably honour the Indian pilot."Smit Machchhar deserves every bit of appreciation, for he embodied the meaning of courage and responsibility in the face of a dangerous terrorist act and a potential disaster," said Gargash in a post in Arabic on X.Captain Smit Machchharâs professionalism and moral sense in the darkest of circumstances make him a true hero, UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash said. The remarks seemed intended to reassure the international community that local institutions will actively confront extremist threats and also conduct the probe into the attack with absolute transparency.âFar from the easy reduction of what happened or the adoption and promotion of conspiracy theories, vigilance and caution remain essential in confronting the risks of extremism and terrorism,â Gargash said.In India, Azar said Israeli people were grateful to Machchhar, calling him a true hero of India.âThose who help Israel are never forgotten by Israel. I can assure you that Machchhar will be honoured and recognised in Israel. I have no doubt about that,â said the Israeli ambassador, adding that Israel doesnât forget people who help the country.âHe demonstrated through his calmness, determination, and experience that terrorism can be defeated,â he said in his remarks to News-18.

World.title: To counter China, India formally puts Gogra, Hot Spring & others on map
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In what is intended to remove any ambiguity or misplaced perception regarding certain land areas, peaks, mountains, passes, glaciers and water bodies in Ladakh, including those bordering China, being an integral part of India, the government has, in consultation with the UT, identified 28 places and features in Ladakh by standard names on the official map of the Survey of India.

Among the 28 are places in Aksai Chin and Gilgit-Baltistan in POK, which India treats as part of Ladakh.

"Identifying them formally... is aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the people at large," the home ministry said Friday.

The move comes less than a couple of months after a similar step was taken with regard to 27 border areas and passes in Arunachal Pradesh.

Among the 28 places in Ladakh identified are 10 peaks, three mountains, seven land areas, two glaciers, two passes, one river, one lake, one water body and one valley.

The list includes Hot Spring and Gogra, which were friction points during the 2020 standoff between India and China.

The list also has Alisha Giri; Brangsa; Chapchingal Pass; Kanishka Peak; Karun Pir mountain; Kuksel; Martand Giri; Parpik Glacier; Skamri Glacier; Shachmirik Pass; Shkorga Valley; Zorawar Peak; Dehra Compass; and Drak Karpo.

Jolmori; Kumarayana Point; Panglung; Rinchen Zangpo; Sakyasri Giri; Guru Rinpoche; Shamal Lungpa (a patrol and staging route in the 1950s); Yangpa River; Marpa Lotsava Ri; Milarepa Kangri; Shiva Ri, and Maheshwara Ri have also been identified.

China has repeatedly staked its claim on border areas in Ladakh and Arunachal, even calling locations in the latter by Chinese names. India has strongly rejected these claims.

World.title: Unsolicited advice to Supreme Court lands trial judge in trouble
World.content:
After reading the letter, which was placed before a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran, the court expressed shock over its contents, which were uncalled for and directed its registry to ask the judge why he wrote what he wrote.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: It sounds inconceivable that a trial judge will advise the top court of the country on how to decide a case. But it happened recently, and the judge is now in trouble, with the Supreme Court seeking an explanation from him for advising it on when to grant bail.The case pertains to the bail petition of an accused from West Bengal who has been an undertrial prisoner for the last five years, and the apex court, while rejecting his plea, had asked the trial court to complete the proceedings within three months. The order, which was passed on May 11, directed the trial court to file a report after disposal of the case.As the trial court could not honour the SC order, the judge wrote to the apex court seeking more time to conclude the trial. But the judge, the additional district and sessions judge, 3rd court, North 24 Parganas at Barasat, also gave some unsolicited advice to the apex court on bail jurisprudence - when to grant bail and when not.After reading the letter, which was placed before a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran, the court expressed shock over its contents, which were uncalled for and directed its registry to ask the judge why he wrote what he wrote.The bench, however, did not reveal the exact wording of the letter but noted in its order that the judge conveyed words of advice."We are quite disturbed with the manner in which the trial judge has addressed a letter to this court requesting some more time. It is not for the presiding officer to convey words of advice as to when this court should grant bail and should not grant bail. The last two paragraphs of the letter are something which we have not appreciated. Registry to call for an appropriate explanation from the presiding officer at the earliest," SC said.The judge had written the letter dated Aug 11 addressed to the assistant registrar, Supreme Court, and prayed for some more time to complete the trial. Fixing the time for completion of the trial, SC in May had noted the case was proceeding at a snail's pace and asked that the trial be expedited as the accused had been languishing in jail for the last five years.Referring to a Calcutta HC order which had rejected the bail plea in March, saying all witnesses would be examined by the end of April, SC had said in its May order, "Although the HC was quite confident the remaining 12 witnesses would be examined by May 1, yet it seems not a single witness has been examined... We give one last chance to the state to proceed further with the recording of evidence of the remaining witnesses. We direct the trial court to see to it that the trial is completed within three months from today without fail."

World.title: Can't invoke anti-slaughter law in case of mere illegal cattle transportation: SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: At a time when vigilante groups are active in stopping cattle smuggling purportedly to prevent slaughter, the Supreme Court has ruled that the police cannot presumptively invoke stringent provisions of anti-cattle slaughter laws against people for mere illegal transportation of bovine animals.

Acquitting a person convicted by a trial court and Chhattisgarh HC for illegally transporting 32 bulls under Chhattisgarh Agricultural Cattle Preservation Act, 2004, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said police have failed to establish the intention of the accused that cattle were being transported for slaughter. The prosecution said the intercepted truck did not have any document that authorised the driver and cleaner to transport cattle from Chhattisgarh to Odisha.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"The mere fact that the transport was not accompanied by any documents cannot lead to a presumption that it was for slaughter," SC said. "We find no reason to uphold the conviction, especially when a veterinary doctor and the 'Gaushala Committee' chief said before the court that the seized cattle were fit for use in agriculture."

World.title: Asian Games 2026 LIVE: Archer Kumkum wins historic recurve gold at Asian Games, earns Olympic quota

Teenager Kumkum Mohod kept her composure under pressure to clinch gold in the women’s individual recurve event at the Asian Games, defeating South Korea’s Oh Yejin in a shoot-out. With the victory, Kumkum became the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games medal in the individual recurve event.

She had also secured an Olympic quota place for India by reaching the semifinals, defeating China’s Jingyi Zhu 6-2.

World.title: Several injured in Australia as car crashes into crowd north of Sydney

World.title: ‘Vettri Payanam’ scheme launched in Madurai
World.content:
Madurai Collector Nishant Krishna launched the expansion of the ‘Vettri Payanam’ scheme at the MGR bus stand in Mattuthavani on Friday. A total of 705 buses will be operated under the scheme.

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay launched the ‘Vettri Payanam’ scheme expanding no-fare bus travel for women and transgender persons, at the Koyambedu bus terminus in Chennai.

Under the expanded ‘Vettri Payanam’ scheme, women and transgender persons can undertake no fare travel on the Ordinary, Express, Limited Stop Service, and Deluxe government buses operating in cities and towns and on the Ordinary buses operating in mofussil areas and hill routes.

Under the scheme, a total of 705 buses comprising 665 city buses (405 Ordinary, 64 Express, and 196 Deluxe) and 40 Mofussil buses operated by Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (TNSTC Madurai Zone) will be operated.

MLAs A. Kallanai, S.R. Thangapandi, Madhar Badhurudeen, Deputy Mayor T. Nagarajan, Corporation Commissioner Gaurav Kumar, Managing Director of TNSTC (Madurai) V. Saravanan, General Manager J. Balamurugan and others were present at the event.

A district administration press release said the ‘Vettri Payanam’ scheme was implemented on Gandhi Jayanti with the main objective of ensuring social and economic independence of women. It would give them easy access to bus service for education, employment and medical needs.

World.title: Asian Games 2026 India’s medallists: Full list of winners
World.content:
The 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games are underway in Japan. India is currently placed at the 5th spot on the medals’ table with 76 medals. China is leading the table with 317 medals. Japan is second with 240 medals and Republic of Korea is third with 134 medals.

The trio of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti, and Kumkum Anil Mohod shocked powerhouses South Korea to win India’s first-ever Asian Games gold in the Women’s Team Recurve event.

Olympic medalist Lovlina Borgohain won the gold medal in the Women’s 75kg division, becoming only the second Indian female boxer in history to secure an Asiad gold. Kumkum Anil Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara claimed a hard-fought silver in the Recurve Mixed Team event. Compound archer Ganesh Mani Ratnam Thirumuru won men’s individual bronze.

India’s Dharmveer Chaudhary, Manu T.S., Jay Kumar and Vishal T.K. clinched the bronze medal in the men’s 4x400m relay at the Asian Games.

India’s Sunil Kumar clinched bronze in the Greco-Roman 87kg category at the Asian Games 2026, becoming the first Indian Greco-Roman wrestler to win two medals at the Games.

Kynan Darius Chenai and Neeru Dhanda staged a superb comeback to beat Qatar and claim gold in the trap mixed team event. The Indian pair finished with an Asian-record score of 34, securing India’s third gold medal of the day.

India edged China 238-237 to clinch gold in the men’s compound archery event, completing a clean sweep of all three compound events. Earlier, the women’s team of Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Prithika Pradeep and Chikitha Taniparthi defeated China to win gold, while India beat South Korea in a shoot-off in the mixed team final to seal another gold and secure a place at the LA 2028 Olympics.

Indian boxer Priya Ghanghas signed off with a bronze medal after going down to former world champion China’s Yang Chengyu in the 60kg semifinal and similarly, Kapil Pokhariya bowed out with a bronze medal after losing 1-4 to Uzbekistan’s Turabek Khabibullaev in the men’s 90kg semifinal.

On Tuesday (September 29, 2026), the quartet of Kiran Pahal, M.R. Poovamma, Prachi Choudhary and Vithya Ramraj won India’s first and only track-and-field gold medal at the Asian Games in Nagoya.

Indian boxer Narender Berwal won the men’s +90kg bronze medal at the 2026 Asian Games after losing to reigning world champion Aibek Oralbay of Kazakhstan in the semi-finals on Tuesday (September 30, 2026).

Gulveer Singh added a third medal to his tally at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, clinching bronze in the men’s 5000m on Tuesday.

India’s mixed 4x100m relay quartet of Gurindervir Singh, Sneha S.S., Animesh Kujur and Harita Bhadra clinched bronze at the Asian Games.

India’s Pooja Singh secured the bronze medal in the women’s high jump at the 2026 Asian Games on Tuesday after clearing 1.84m in the final.

The quartet of Manu T.S., Dharmveer Choudhary, Jay Kumar and Vishal T.K. clinched bronze in the men’s 4x400m relay final on Tuesday.

Neeru Dhanda scripted history on Tuesday (September 29, 2026), becoming the first Indian shooter to win an Asian Games gold medal in the women’s individual trap event, while also breaking the continental record in the process.

Indian shooters Neeru Dhanda, Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer clinched silver in the women’s trap team event at the Asian Games.

On September 28, 2026, Vithya Ramraj won a bronze medal in 400 M hurdles in a sensational run that clocked 54.75 seconds and broke her own national record she had jointly held with athlete PT Usha.

Murali Sreeshankar and Gulveer Singh claimed silver medals in the long jump and 1500m, respectively, while Parul Chaudhary secured bronze in the women’s 5000m, adding a second medal to her Aichi-Nagoya campaign.

India also bagged two medals in the javelin throw, with Yash Vir Singh winning silver and Rohit Yadav taking bronze, behind Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga.

Earlier that day, Indian shooter Esha Singh clinched a silver medal in the women’s 25m pistol individual competition.

Pincky Balhara became the first Indian to win two Kurash medals at the Asian Games after clinching bronze on Monday (September 28, 2026), following a 0-5 semifinal defeat to South Korea’s Sumin Mo in the women’s 78kg event.

On Sunday (September 27, 2026), India’s Abhay Singh settled for an Asian Games silver medal after going down against Eain Yow Ng of Malaysia in the men’s singles final of the squash competition, and junior world champion Anahat Singh similarly secured a hard-fought Silver in the women’s singles final against Malaysia’s Sivasangari Subramaniam.

Harita Bhadra clinched bronze in the women’s 200m at the Asian Games. Long jumper Ancy Sojan secured silver in the women’s long jump, while Sarvesh Kushare claimed silver in the men’s high jump.

Tejaswin Shankar, meanwhile, secured his second Asian Games medal, winning bronze in the decathlon following the two-day competition.

Parul Chaudhary bettered her personal best on her way to bronze in the women’s 3000m steeplechase at the Asian Games.

On Saturday (September 26), India’s Sawan Barwal won a silver medal in the men’s marathon. India’s women’s kabaddi team extended their dominance at the Asian Games securing yet another gold medal after a thrilling 37-34 win over Iran in the finals. The men’s hockey team continued it’s winning streak, defeating Japan by 2-0, securing the semifinal berth in the big-ticket sports event.

Simultaneously, the squash squad led by teen-sensation Anahat Singh and Abhay Shetty in singles category stormed into the final game. The duo will be competing for a gold medal in their final game on Sunday.

Women’s 50m rifle 3P team comprising of Vidarsa Vinod, Ashi Chouksey, Tilottama Sen won the silver medal. Mixed squash doubles team including Joshana Chinappa, Velavan Senthilkumar clinched the bronze medal.

On Friday (September 25), the duo of Manush Shah and Diya Chitale secured a historic bronze medal in table tennis mixed doubles after stunning the world No. 4 pair from Hong Kong to enter the semi-finals.

Baranica Elangovan entered her name in the record books by winning a historic bronze medal for India in the women’s pole vault event at the Asian Games

Indian long-distance runner Gulveer Singh upgraded his Asian Games medal from bronze to silver in the men’s 10,000m.

India’s Manpreet Kaur clinched the bronze medal in women’s shot put competition of the Asian Games with an effort of 17.17m in Nagoya on Friday (September 25).

Kamaljeet and Suruchi Singh won gold in the mixed team 10m air pistol event. The Indian team, comprising Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar, Rudranksh Patil and Niraj Kumar, won silver in the men’s 50m rifle 3P team event.

The Indian 4x400m mixed relay quartet of Vishal T.K., M.R. Poovamma, Manu T.S. and Vithya Ramraj earned a silver medal in the final at the Paloma Mizuho Stadium.

Manpreet Kaur clinched a bronze medal in the Women’s Shot Put final with a season-best throw of 17.17 meters.

The duo of Manush Shah and Diya Chitale secured a historic bronze in Table Tennis Mixed Doubles after stunning the world No. 4 pair from Hong Kong to enter the semi-finals.

Seema Kumari, competing in her first Asiad, won a bronze medal in the 10,000m at the Asian Games, 16 years after Preeja Sreedharan and Kavita Raut’s historic gold-silver double in 2010.

Manipur’s Naorem Roshibina Devi won her third consecutive Asian Games medal, clinching silver after losing to Zhang Xiaoyu in the women’s 60kg wushu final on Thursday (September 24, 2026).

Jay Meena secured India’s first-ever soft tennis medal at the Asian Games, fetching a bronze after losing to Japan’s Takuya Kurosaka in the men’s singles semifinals. Star Indian weightlifter Mirabai Chanu completed her medal collection, winning a silver medal in the women’s 49kg event in the Asian Games.

Lakshya Sen and Ayush Shetty faltered against higher-ranked opponents as the Indian men’s team concluded with a bronze medal after losing 1-3 to their rivals, China, in the semifinals.

The Indian Women’s Cricket Team clinched a historic victory at the Karogi Athletic Park in Nisshin, Aichi. Facing off against Sri Lanka in a high-stakes final, the Women in Blue triumphed to secure India’s very first gold medal of the tournament.

Meanwhile, shooters have led the charge for India. The women’s skeet team, comprising Raiza Dhillon, Maheshwari Chauhan and Parinaaz Dhaliwal, won a bronze with a combined score of 331 here on September 23, 2026.

Experienced rifle shooter Elavenil Valarivan played a starring role in the country’s double-silver haul in the women’s 10m air rifle competition. Elavenil, one of India’s most accomplished rifle shooters, helped the country secure silver in the team event along with Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod. She then went on to add an individual silver.

For the men’s side, teenager Himanshu Dhillon produced a superb performance to win silver, while former world champion Rudrankksh Patil clinched bronze as India secured two individual podium finishes in the men’s 10m air rifle event. The two then teamed up with Parth Mane to win another silver in the team event, finishing just behind China.

After an impressive start in shooting, India also managed to script history in Mixed Martial Arts (MMA), with Suchika Tariyal winning the nation’s first-ever bronze medal for MMA at the Asian Games.

A contingent of 501 Indian athletes, comprising 267 men and 234 women, is competing across 36 disciplines in the 2026 edition. Apart from shooting, athletics and archery too are expected to add to the medal tally. India is also defending both the men’s and women’s titles in cricket and kabaddi.
